In contrast, in the Mahayana scriptures of the middle period, the human nature thought of the physical aspect stands out.Regarding the clean human nature, in ‘Vimalakirti Sutra’, the beonnwejeukbori thought appears. The origin is the Yeorae Sect and the Buddhist sect. Regarding ‘Avatamsaka Sutra’, while emphasizing the seonggi thought, it emphasized that it does not know about the possession of the wisdom and the virtue of the Tathagata on the part of all living beings. [This point is similar to ‘the Seungman Sutra’ and ‘the Tathagatagarbha Sutra’.] In the third, in ‘the Seungman Sutra’, ilbulseung is put forth. As the aspect that all people attain Buddhahood, the sugi has been emphasized. Regarding ‘the Yeoraejang Scripture’ that pertains to the Mahayana Sutras in the middle period has been preaching the Tathagatagarbha. And ‘the Neungga Scripture’ has been preaching the jagakseongji thought. The scripture that had the biggest influence on the establishment of the Zen thought is ‘the Yeolban Scripture’. In this scripture, while saying that there is the Buddha nature in all of the people, it said that the most foolish icchantikas, too, attain Buddhahood. And the women and the evil persons attain Buddhahood. And it said that even the heartless people attain Buddhahood.From after Dharma arrived in China, while the Zen thought was established, the Zen sect was formed. While, mostly, the Zen sect had developed into many schools, regarding the Zen masters of the initial Zen sect, by accommodating the bongak and human nature thought, the Zen thought of the faction of the side was established.

articles.title_kr: 이통현 육상설의 특징과 의의
articles.title_en: Features and Significance of Li Tongxuan's Theory of the Six Characteristics (六相說)
articles.abstract_kr: This study explores Li Tongxuan's distinctive interpretation and characteristics of the Six Characteristics Theory (六相說), a core doctrine of East Asian Huayan Buddhism. While previous research remains at a basic level of understanding regarding Li Tongxuan's Six Characteristics Theory, this paper delves deeper to analyze its application, purpose, and structural features, aiming to identify its unique aspects and significance.Li Tongxuan inherited the Six Characteristics Theory from Uisang and Fazang, applying it comprehensively to all phenomena of dependent origination (緣起) and elucidating its essence as unobstructed interpenetration (無礙圓融). However, he does not merely follow their framework; instead, he creatively transforms it, establishing a unique interpretation of the Six Characteristics Theory. Specifically, Li introduces novel perspectives such as the application of the Six Characteristics between doctrinal and practical realms (教法-事法) and the self-application of the Six Characteristics Theory itself, breaking away from the traditional internal structure to propose a more expansive and flexible model.Through these transformations, Li Tongxuan builds an original interpretation of the Six Characteristics Theory, while actively inheriting and developing the theories of Uisang and Fazang through doctrinal reinterpretation and application. This continuity and originality position Li Tongxuan's Six Characteristics Theory as a unique contribution to the intellectual history of East Asian Huayan Buddhism.

articles.title_kr: 원효의 불성유무 화쟁과 일심과의 관계에 대한 연구
articles.title_en: A Study on the Relationship between Wonhyo’s reconciliation of disputes on the Buddha-nature and One Mind
articles.abstract_kr: We looked at the arguments and refutations about the existence of Buddha-nature in Wonhyo's Reconciliation of Disputes in Ten Aspects (十門和諍論). In addition, Wonhyo's reconciliation of disputes was examined, and the relationship between reconciliation of disputes and one One-Mind was examined.In the Reconciliation of Disputes in Ten Aspects, Wonhyo appears to describe the debate and reconciliation of disputes from the perspective of the existence of Buddha-nature, and in the Nirvana Jongyo(涅槃宗要), reconciliation of disputes is discussed from the perspective of the body of Buddha-nature. From the point of view of the existence of Buddha-nature and from the point of view of the body of Buddha-nature, Wonhyo is using the logic of reconciliation of disputes through the aspect of Eui-ji(依持門) and the aspect of Yeon-gi(緣起門). The five-gotras discrimination theory, which uses the natural-pure-seed as the body of Buddha-nature, is reconciled through the aspect of Eui-ji(依持門), and the theory that all beings become Buddhas, which uses Bhūtatathatā as the body of Buddha-nature, is reconciled through the aspect of Yeon-gi(緣起門). It is the position of ordinary categories to considers the natural-pure-seed as the body of Buddha, and it is the position of truthful categories to consider Bhūtatathatā as the body of Buddha.However, Wonhyo sees the body of Buddha-nature with One-Mind. From the point of view of One-Mind, the two arguments are correct in that they partially reveal Buddha-nature. However, since the two arguments do not fully reveal Buddha nature, the two arguments are said to be wrong. In the end, if One-Mind is viewed as the body of Buddha-nature, it is neither wrong nor right.What is the significance of Wonhyo's reconciliation of disputes about Buddha-nature while looking at the body of Buddha-nature with One-mind in modern society? Today, it seems that modern society is mass-producing sentient beings with diverse and complex mental structures. At this point, the significance of the reconciliation of disputes between the theory of five-gotras discrimination and the theory that all beings become Buddhas is that the two arguments act as a practical method from the perspective of One-Mind. In other words, both arguments correspond to ways to lead sentient beings to Buddha-nature.
keywords_en: Reconciliation of Disputes in Ten Aspects

articles.title_kr: 大本 般若波羅蜜多心經의 한역과 티벳역 비교 분석
articles.title_en: Comparative Analysis of Chinese Translation & Tibetan Translation of Large version Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya
articles.abstract_kr: There are two main texts in this study: the Chinese translation of 『佛說聖佛母般若波羅蜜多經』(T0257) & the Tibetan translation of bCom ldan 'das ma shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i snying po/(󰡔世尊母般若波羅蜜多經)(d21). These texts belong to Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya of Large version.The main purpose of this study is to compare and analyze the contents of these two texts. The main part consists of four paragraphs, namely, an overview of Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya, Original text of Chinese Translation & Tibetan Translation of this Sutra and its Korean Translation, and a comparative analysis of the contents of two texts.In addition, the comparative analysis of the contents of two texts is divided into eight sub-items, namely, The name of the Sutra, The expression ‘佛說’ or ‘聖’ at the beginning of the name of the sutra, Format of Beginning and End of Two texts, the number of Bhikkhu in Historical introduction, the meaning of ‘智慧(Shes rab/)’ and ‘Ye shes/’, the addition of the letter ‘Oṃ/’ to Prajñāpāramitā Mantra, the interpretation of ‘世間('Jig rten/)’ in Conclusion, and the adoption of Terminology including the name of Samādhi.In this way, it is hoped that this study will provide new information for a clear understanding of the profound meaning of Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya as well as for recognizing the differences in content between two texts, and will serve as an opportunity to broaden the horizons of future research on this matter.
keywords_en: Bhodhisattva Mahāsattva the noble lord Avalokiteśvara

articles.title_kr: 대승불교의 계율 옹호론에 대하여 - 『菩薩地』 「眞實義品」에 나타난 소승계 수계의 근거 -
articles.title_en: On the Defense of Monastic Precepts in Mahayana Buddhism - The Theoretical Basis for Accepting Vinaya in the Bodhisattvabhūmi -
articles.abstract_kr: This study aimed to explore the theoretical basis for the acceptance of the monastic rule(Vinaya) among Mahāyānists by examining the “Tattvārthapaṭala” chapter in Bodhisattvabhūmi which is presented by the Yogācāra school. The result of this reseach can be summarized as follows:The Prajñāpāramitāsūtras explicitly state that a bodhisattva should not adhere to the precepts(śīla) of the two vehicles. This reflects the general stance of Mahāyāna Buddhism, which upholds non-self-nature (anātman) or the emptiness(śūnyatā) as their main assertion, ignores the monastic rules.However, while the “Tattvārthapaṭala” in the Bodhisattvabhūmi accepts the doctrine of emptiness as well, this text restricts its interpretation to mean “the absence of intrinsic nature in linguistic expressions,” emphasizing the reality of the basis (vastu) or, the suchness (tathatā).. This perspective critiques the Madhyamaka school’s negation of foundational reality by categorizing it as “misapprehension of emptiness” (durgṛhītā-śūnyatā).It argues that such a misapprehension undermines the monastic traditions and impedes practice; thus, it posits that a practitioner of the Lesser Vehicle, who may hold notions of self (satkāyadṛṣṭi), is preferable to some Mahāyānists with a flawed understanding of emptiness. Furthermore, while ultimate truth transcends by linguistic expressions only, the āgama, as conveyed through transmitted scriptures, are affirmed for their practical efficacy. This modified truth discourse allowed the Yogācāra school to actively integrate the established systems of monastic tradition.

articles.title_kr: 6.25전쟁 시기의 불교 선승들의 동향에 관한 고찰 - 선원 방함록을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: A Study on the Activities of Buddhist Seon Masters during the Korean War (June 25, 1950) - Focusing on the Seonwon Banghamrok -
articles.abstract_kr: This paper analyzes the activities of Korean Seon masters who dedicated themselves to practice while protecting the essence of Buddhism during the harsh conditions of the Korean War (June 25, 1950) and considers their effects on the modern Korean Buddhism. During the war, many Seon masters migrated south, with Geumjeongsa, Beomeosa, and Seonamsa temples in Busan emerging as key centers for their activities. These circumstances are confirmed through the Banghamrok on Seon Centers and related testimonies. This study analyzes the activities of Seon masters and changes in their practice environments during the war, focusing on Banghamrok on Seon Centers. By analyzing the 『Geumjeongsa Banghamrok on Seon Centers』 and the 「Beomeosa Banghamrok on Seon Centers」, among others, it will explore the war’s impact on the traditions and practices of Seon centers and analyze Seonamsa and other key sites without available Banghamrok records based on testimonies. As a result, this study confirmed that during the Korean War, Seon masters strengthened their unity through practice and interaction and based thereon, laid a crucial foundation for the continuity and development of modern Korean Buddhism. This study reminds us that the efforts of Seon masters to preserve the essence of Buddhism even in the harsh circumstances of the war provide valuable lessons for contemporary Buddhists and that it is important to maintain the essence of Buddhism and continue practice even in any adversity.

articles.title_kr: 간화선의 보편적 적용을 위한 심리치료적 작용기제 고찰
articles.title_en: An Investigation on the Mechanism of Psychotherapeutic Functions for the Universal Application of Ganhwa Seon
articles.abstract_kr: Meditation is attracting attention as a representative measure for the mental and physical health of modern people, and it is actively developing in connection with various Buddhist-based meditation practices and social studies such as psychology. Accordingly, in order to approach Ganhwa Seon(Chan, Zen) as a popular practice method, this paper interpreted the structure and principles of Ganhwa Seon practice in terms of the psychotherapeutic function mechanism within the category of meditation psychology.First, the word, ‘gan’(看, literally, watch (a hwadu)), in Ganhwa Seon encompasses the function of mindfulness (sati, 念), while enhancing the function of concentration and insight through the process of doubt. Based on the internal effect of psychological stability caused by mindfulness, the hwadu doubt has functionally a structure that quickly leads to the hwadu samadhi through the method of concurrent cultivation of samādhi and prajñā(定慧雙修).Second, hwadu investigation which constitutes the core of Ganhwa Seon promotes the arising of doubt through the functions of attention shift and discriminatory consciousness. At the moment of hwadu investigation, the exercise of ‘gan’ primarily separates from unhealthy psychological states and causes conversion to internal insight. At this time the discriminatory consciousness that conflicts with general thoughts leads to the mechanism of doubt. Even if doubt does not arise strongly, it can be expected to have the effect of inducing a shift in attention to the observer’s point of view of metacognition and strengthening his or her own identity and subjectivity.Third, the awareness of problems raised by hwadu investigation that has settled within the practitioner is diverse, ranging from matters facing in daily life to essential inner troubles. The question of what is ‘this’ encompasses horizontal spreading and vertical deepening, and can be applied as a psychological mechanism that connects everyday affairs to a fundamental inner question.

articles.title_kr: 만해 한용운의 불성 사상과 공약삼장
articles.title_en: Manhae Han Yong-un’s Doctrine of Buddha-Nature and the “Three Articles of the Agreement”
articles.abstract_kr: This paper examines how Manhae Han Yong-un’s doctrine of Buddha-nature (佛性) was philosophically reflected in the “Three Articles of the Agreement” (公約三章), an appendix to the Declaration of Independence proclaimed during the March 1st Independence Movement. In his Treatise on the Reformation of Korean Buddhism (朝鮮佛敎維新論), Manhae sought to reinterpret the concept of Buddha-nature within a framework of modern thought. While referencing Kant’s concept of freedom through the works of Liang Qichao, he ultimately embraced and transcended such ideas from the standpoint of Patriarchal Seon (祖師禪). Manhae emphasized the original equality and autonomy inherent in all beings through the concepts of sudden enlightenment (頓悟) and the realization of freedom, understanding Buddha-nature not as an external metaphysical idea but as the inherent, free, and equal true self (自性) within each individual.This line of thought is concretely embodied in the “Three Articles of the Agreement,” which Manhae is believed to have directly drafted. The first article presents the values of justice, humanity, survival, and dignity, along with an emphasis on a “spirit of freedom,” reflecting his interpretation of Buddha-nature as the manifestation of freedom. The second article can be seen as a natural ethical imperative derived from the concepts of “freedom” and “independence” discussed in the first, while the third article, with its call to “respect order,” metaphorically embodies the spirit of nonviolence.Furthermore, Manhae’s Song of Enlightenment(悟道頌), composed after attaining awakening through Seon practice, symbolizes the realization of freedom, the transcendence of conditioned causality (緣起), and the recognition of one’s original face. It is not merely a personal expression of insight, but a declaration that seeks to awaken the times through a spirit of self-mastery amidst historical darkness. Thus, this study reinterprets the “Three Articles of the Agreement” not simply as a practical guideline for the independence movement, but as a philosophical declaration grounded in Buddhist ontology and ethics of practice, presenting Manhae’s thought as a living philosophy of self-realization and liberation still relevant today.

articles.title_kr: 「님의 침묵」에서 ‘침묵’의 사상적 배경: 불이법문  - 만해의 『유마힐소설경강의』를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: The Theoretical Background of 'the Silence' in "My Lord's Silence": The Teaching of Non-duality - Focused on Manhae's Lecture on the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra -
articles.abstract_kr: This paper explores the meaning of the silence in Manhae's representative poem, "My Lord's Silence". Manhae has written the Lecture on the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra, which features the 'Vimalakirti's Silence'. This contains Manhae's views on the teaching of non-duality, which can be said to be the background of silence. The results on the book are as follows.First, we looked at the teaching of non-duality spoken at the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra. If silence is at the aspect of Seon(禪), it can be said that the teaching of non-duality is at the aspect of Teachings(敎). The teaching of non-duality refers to the middle way which is based on the theory of dependent origination. This teaching can be seen in most part of the sūtra.Second, through Manhae's commentary on the sūtra, we examined the vivid appearance of the teaching. In the third and fourth chapter, there are scenes in which the Buddha's disciples explain the lessons heard from Vimalakirti in the past. It was confirmed that through Manhae's commentary, he revealed the various types of teaching of non-duality in such lessons.And third, we paid attention to Manhae's commentary on the establishment and practice of the teaching of non-duality. In the fifth chapter, Vimalakirti discusses how a bodhisattva attains a peaceful mind. Manhae showed in the commentary that the teaching has been established through three steps and has been practiced from a passive attitude to an active attitude.
keywords_en: The Lecture on the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra

articles.title_kr: 증각 홍척(證覺 洪陟)과 실상산문(實相山門)의 선풍에 관한 고찰
articles.title_en: A Study on the Seon Style of Jeung-gak Hongcheok and Silsangsanmun
articles.abstract_kr: 본 연구의 목적은 구산선문 중 하나인 실상산문을 개창한 증각 홍척과 그를 계승한 실상산문 선사들이 보여준 선풍의 특징을 파악하여, 한국 선사상사에서의 위상을 재정립하는 데 있다. 서당 지장에게 남종선을 배운 뒤 신라로 돌아온 홍척은 왕실의 후원 아래 실상사를 중심으로 가장 먼저 선문을 열고 활동하였다. 그의 제자 수철은 왕실과의 교류를 지속하며 실상산문의 발전을 이끌었다. 홍척과 수철에게서 나타나는 실상산문의 사상 경향을 선과 교학, 민간신앙, 현실 참여가 조화롭게 결합된 선풍으로 요약할 수 있다. 이들은 당시 불교계의 주류였던 화엄 교학을 받아들여 선과 교를 겸비했는데, 그 배경에는 서당의 가풍에 대한 계승 의식이 작용했던 것으로 보인다. 또한 산악신앙과 같은 민간신앙적 요소를 배척하지 않고 선법을 전파하는 방편으로 활용했으며, 전법교화의 일환으로서 궁중 설법과 철불 조성 등 현실 참여적 활동을 전개하기도 했다. 홍척을 비롯한 실상산문 선사들은 한국선에서 선교겸수를 표방한 선구적 사례이자, 민간신앙 포용과 현실 참여를 통해 선법의 안착 및 유포에 기여한 공로자들이었다.
keywords_en: combined practice of Seon and Gyo

articles.title_kr: 『본지풍광』「염화미소」화의 수시게송에 대한 시론적 독해
articles.title_en: A Study on The teaching as a Preface(垂示) from “The Story of Have one mind(拈花微笑)”, the second chapter of The Scenery of the true heart(本地風光)
articles.abstract_kr: This study is on The teaching as a Preface(垂示) from “The Story of Have one mind(拈花微笑)”, the second chapter of The Scenery of the true heart(本地風光). In the story, when Shakyamuni Buddha raises a flower, Mahākāśyapa smiles. Shakyamuni then declares that he will transmit the Buddha's true Dharma seal and the subtle mind of Nirvana to Kāśyapa. This event serves as the focal point for discussing the Buddha's mind, and the study aims to interpret this story. The reason for focusing on The teaching as a Preface(垂示), because it is emphasized as containing the core message that Master Seongcheol wished to convey.In this study, The hundred days of sermons(百日法門) and he True Path to Zen Enlightenment(禪門正路) are essential references, as they are presented in a logical language. The language of Zen masters often reflects the paradoxical nature of reality, or the simultaneous coexistence of seemingly contradictory aspects. This paradoxical language is the best means to convey the reality witnessed in the state of enlightenment. However, all language can only exist when dividing the indivisible reality into two, which is why The Harmony of Truth becomes necessary.There are two kinds of The Harmony of Truth: one in which the roles of subject and object are separated, unfolding between the interaction of characters; and another linguistic The Harmony of Truth called profound expressions or subtle words(玄言妙句). When the Buddha shows one, Mahākāśyapa responds with two. Through this mutual collaboration, the simultaneous manifestation of wholeness and differentiation occurs. Linguistic collaboration is carried out through poetic parallelism, illogical reasoning, or the fusion with the environment. It holds contradictory aspects together in a unified view. In this way, it reveals the profound truth that the non-self that lets go of the ego is, in fact, the complete revival of all discriminations. Most typically, as seen in the The Story of Have one mind, it is the collaboration between the master and the disciple, or between fellow practitioners. It is also a performance revealing the interdependent arising of the dharma realm, where all things and events are interrelated and rely on each other for their existence.
keywords_en: The Scenery of the true heart(本地風光)
The Story of Have one mind(拈花微笑)
The hundred days of sermons(百日法門)
True Path to Zen Enlightenment(禪門正路)

articles.title_kr: 백봉 김기추의 간화선 체험과 선사상적 특징에 대한 고찰
articles.title_en: A Study on Baekbong Kim Gichu’s Enlightenment of Ganhwaseon and the Characteristics of his Seon thought
articles.abstract_kr: In this study, I examined Baekbong Kim Gichu’s experience of Ganhwaseon and the Characteristics of his Seon thought. First, I discussed Baekbong’s Ganhwaseon experience in relation to the three essentials - Great Faith, Great Determination, and Great Doubt - which are emphasized in the Ganhwaseon tradition. Although Baekbong knew little about the theory and ideology of Seon, and even the methodology of Ganhwaseon, I were able to discover the contents corresponding to The three essentials of Ganhwaseon: Great Faith, Great Determination, and Great Doubt in his experience. Second, I examined the characteristics of his Seon thought centered on ‘emptiness of subtle existence’ and ‘Sentient beings Buddha.’ In this study, I focused on examining these characteristics in detail and examining the basis for these discussions from the standpoint of Seon literature and Seon thought. Baekbong emphasizes that the nature of our mind itself is void-calm, and that although it is emptiness of subtle existence, it itself has a divine knowledge, that is, ‘Numinous-Awareness.’ Also, Baekbong frequently used the term ‘Sentient beings Buddha’ to emphasize that one should practice from the standpoint of Buddha, seeing that many people think of themselves as humble and incompetent. Thirdly, I examined his view of Ganhwaseon focusing on ‘Saemaulgwi’. ‘Saemaulgwi’ means ‘New-Hwadu’ and can be said to be a kind of transformation and reform of the traditional Hwadu. This Saemaulgwi is Baekbong’s transformation of the existing Hwadu centered on monks, He changed that anyone can practice it. This is a substitute for the traditional Ganhwaseon, and it is practiced based on faith in Dharma-kāya rather than doubting the Hwadu.

articles.title_kr: 고려전기 의천 편정(編定) 원종문류의 집일(輯佚) 및 유문(類門)
articles.title_en: Textual reconstruction(輯佚) and Categorical Sections (類門) of the Wonjong-Munryu, Edited by Uicheon in the Early Goryeo Period
articles.abstract_kr: This study investigates the current preservation status, textual reconstruction, and analysis of the categorical sections of Wonjong-Munryu, an essential Huayan Buddhist reference compiled by the Goryeo Uicheon. Presently, only three complete volumes survive: only three volumes(Vol. 1, 14, 22). Partial reconstruction has been made possible through materials preserved abroad. It can be partially reconstructed through citations in Chinese and Japanese Buddhist commentaries from the 12th to 14th centuries. Key sources include Cheongjipgi (聽集記), Simuicho (深意鈔), and manuscripts from Kanazawa Bunko(金澤文庫), which preserve citations of texts otherwise lost in East Asia, such as Yonjun’s Yeon'ocho(演奧抄) and Wŏnrang’s Jipseokgi(集釋記).Among the surviving materials of the Wonjong-Munryu, the ones whose volume order and text names are confirmed are “Bonjong Ogyoryu(本宗五敎類)” in Volume 3, “Jemun Jongchwiryu(諸文宗趣類)” in Volume 7, “Jemun Samsaengryu(諸文三生類)” in Volume 20, and “Jemun Byeoljangryu(諸文別章類)” in Volume 21. Also, Volume 4 is “title unknown”, but it is related to doctrinal classification (教判). Next, the texts of the Wonjong-Munryu whose volume order and contents are unknown are Balsimryu(發心類), Danjangryu(斷障類), Sipjijongyoryu(十地宗要類), Bultoryu(佛土類), and Bulsinryu(佛身類).The Wonjong-Munryu has a philological value in that it systematically preserves the Huayan texts that were circulated in the East Asian Buddhist cultural sphere. In addition, the significance lies in the fact that the Wonjong-Munryu can be used to gauge the academic level of Huayan studies in the Goryeo period and the aspects of Buddhist exchange in East Asia.

articles.title_kr: 불교 커뮤니케이션의 학문적 체계 정립을 위한 제언
articles.title_en: Suggestions for an Academic Framework for Buddhist Communication
articles.abstract_kr: This study conducted an in-depth analysis of the SMCRE model (Source, Message, Channel, Receiver, Effect) in communication studies within a Buddhist context. Through this analysis, we explored new methodologies for effectively conveying Buddhist doctrines and teachings in today's rapidly changing society. The research method involved analysing each of the five components of the model individually and examining the interactions between them to derive the overall characteristics and practical implications of the Buddhist message delivery system. Based on this, the concept of Buddhist communication was systematised.Based on the research results, this study proposed the need to train professional communicators, build digital archives, and establish data-based missionary strategies as core tasks for modern Buddhist missionary work. This study is academically significant in that it promotes interdisciplinary research between Buddhist studies and communication studies and establishes a theoretical foundation for Buddhist missionary strategies appropriate for the digital age.

articles.title_kr: 『님의沈默』의 띄어쓰기 양상과 낭송 리듬 분석  - 챗GPT를 활용한 ｢님의沈默｣ 분석을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: An analysis of the spacing patterns and recitation rhythms of “The Silence of the Beloved” -Comparison of Rhythm by Spacing with ChatGPT-
articles.abstract_kr: Marking the 100th anniversary of Manhae's publication of “The Silence of the Beloved”, this study aims to identify the gap between the original text and the edition, which has not been sufficiently illuminated so far. In the case of “The Silence of the Beloved”, unlike other poets, spaces have not been reflected in the process of creating editions. There have been many errors in the process of fixing it in modern language, and discussions have been continuously questioned in these editions. To reveal this, this study carefully reviewed previous studies and looked at discussions on spacing. Based on the '萬海學' that many researchers have accumulated, I would like to pay attention to the problem of spacing that has not yet been revealed, and to guess the cause based on Manhae's thoughts and the context of the times, the meaning of spacing in the original text that is not reflected in the modern version.Therefore, this study confirms that the spacing reflected in “The Silence of the Beloved” is implemented as a language art that closely reflects Manhae's inner rhythm and speech sense. In particular, Manhae's "The Silence of the Beloved" is evaluated as a representative work that combines the language reality of the time, the ideological background, and the nature of formal experimentation. It attempts to understand Manhae's spacing as a subjective expression method that reflects the poet's philosophy, way of thinking, and the literary climate of the time. Furthermore, in this study, the spacing of “The Silence of the Beloved” is viewed as a device for poetic breathing and recitation rhythm, and a recitation-based rhythm analysis is introduced using ChatGPT for analysis to compare and examine the differences between the original and the current edition in detail. Through this, we want to reveal the rhythmic and aesthetic functions performed by spacing in poetry, and to re-examine spacing as an essential element of poetic form.

articles.title_kr: 만해 한용운 한시에 대한 기초적 검토 - 서지 사항과 번역 문제를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: Chronology, Variants, and Translation in the Sino-Korean Poetry(Han-si) of Manhae Han Yong-un
articles.abstract_kr: Although scholarship on Manhae Han Yong-un’s Sino-Korean poetry (han-si) has made some progress, the absence of a foundational critical review has significantly hindered more in-depth research. To address these limitations, this study first examines the bibliographic data, dates of composition, and textual variants of his han-si, and then analyzes issues identified in their translated versions.Regarding bibliographic investigation, this study reconstructs the process through which Manhae’s han-si were compiled. By identifying the sources of his handwritten poetry collection Japjeo (雜著, “Miscellany”) and later compilations, and by comparing them with the extant manuscripts, the study corrects errors that had been introduced in subsequent anthologies.Furthermore, it confirms that the sequence of poems in Japjeo corresponds to their chronological order of composition. This finding is supported by a close reading of Hyangnobongyaeum (香爐庵夜吟, “Night Poem at Hyangno Hermitage”), demonstrating that the chronological arrangement clarifies the interpretive frame of individual works.In the domain of textual comparison, the study shows that mistranslations in Gwannakmaeyugam (觀落梅有感, “Reflections on Falling Plum Blossoms”) can be corrected by consulting its newspaper publication and its later adaptation in sijo form. It also proposes that textual inaccuracies and ambiguities in Jasoshibyeok (自笑詩癖, “Laughing at My Own Poetic Obsession”) can be resolved through intertextual analysis with Manhae’s other han-si and with the works of Park Han-yeong.

articles.title_kr: 원효 화쟁론의 생성존재론적 특성과 현대 차이철학
articles.title_en: Generative-Ontological Characteristics of Wonhyo’s Hwajaeng Theory and Contemporary Philosophies of Difference
articles.abstract_kr: This study aims to clarify the philosophical originality and contemporary significance of Wonhyo’s (617-686) Hwajaeng thought in the context of establishing the identity and global development of Korean Buddhist studies. Wonhyo’s theory of Hwajaeng is not merely a practical mediation between competing doctrinal schools; rather, it constitutes a systematic philosophical framework grounded in the concepts of One Mind (Ilsim) and neither being nor non-being. This research analyzes the hermeneutical features and fourfold negation (Catuṣkoṭi) logic in Wonhyo’s writings and examines their points of resonance with Deleuze’s philosophy of difference and Heidegger’s ontological thought, thereby exploring the possibility of dialogue between Eastern and Western philosophical traditions.Wonhyo’s use of tetralemma to overcome the dichotomy between identity and difference structurally parallels Deleuze’s critique of representation and his notion of univocity. Similarly, the relation of neither-identity-nor-difference between suchness (Tathātā) and arisingand- ceasing within One Mind corresponds to Heidegger’s ontological difference and the event of appropriation (Ereignis). Hwajaeng thought, which affirms difference while seeking interconnection and integration, reveals an inherently dynamic methodology grounded in what may be termed a ‘generative ontology’ - one that emphasizes the dynamic unfolding of being.By situating Wonhyo’s Hwajaeng within these contemporary philosophical contexts, this research seeks to highlight the philosophical potential of Wonhyo’s thought for addressing tensions in today’s pluralistic world and offer significant implications for the global dissemination of Korean Buddhist thought.

articles.title_kr: 원효 계율관의 화쟁적 성격 - 『보살계본지범요기』를 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: The Harmonious Character in Wonhyo's Precepts - Focused on the Essential Note on Observance and Transgression of the Bodhisattva Precepts -
articles.abstract_kr: For the past 60 years, there has been a debate in the academic circle of precept on “Why did Wonhyo write the Essential Note on Observance and Transgression of the Bodhisattva Precepts?” I conducted my own research on this issue, and this paper was written to report the results.First of all, Wonhyo made his precepts clear in the book. In the Introduction, he criticized the actions of people who were biased toward external and selfish actions and declared that he would pursue internal motives and altruistic actions. In the chapter of 'Light and Heavy Transgression', he showed in detail that the evaluation of behavior can be changed by various motives based on the Precepts of Yoga. And in the chapter of 'Deep and Shallow Transgression', he reminded us of the importance of altruistic behavior based on the Precepts of Brahma's Net.Moreover, I applied 3 criteria to determine whether the book has a harmonious character: 'the requirements of harmonization' was met because there were confrontations between people with different views on the precepts; 'the appearances of harmonization' did not seem to be met clearly because it is not a harmonious text; and 'the method of harmonization' was considered to correspond to type 3 since Wonhyo decided that one side was right and the other side was wrong. Taken together, it was judged that the book had a considerable degree of harmonious character.
keywords_en: the Essential Note on Observance and Transgression of the Bodhisattva Precepts

articles.title_kr: 고려후기 백운 경한의 생애와 행적 재검토
articles.title_en: A Reexamination of the Life and Activities of Baekun Gyeonghan in the Late Goryeo Dynasty
articles.abstract_kr: This study reexamined the life and activities of Baegun Gyeonghan (1298-1374), a prominent Buddhist monk of late Goryeo, by synthesizing previous scholarship and reassessing unresolved issues. Although research on Baegun began with the discovery of the Baegun hwasang eorok in the 1930s and the identification of the metal type edition of Jikji simche yojeol in the 1970s, the lack of historical materials has limited comprehensive biographical analysis. This paper classifies his life into four periods: (1) ordination and early activities (1298-1350), (2) pilgrimage to Yuan (1350-1352), (3) propagation after returning to Goryeo (1352-1374), and (4) posthumous commemoration. Baegun devoted himself to meditative practice rather than monastic office after passing the state examination and gained official recognition through public Buddhist services such as the 1346 state rainmaking ritual. This status enabled his state-approved study journey to Yuan in 1350, where he studied under Zhigong in Yuan Dadu(大都) and Shiwu Qinggong(石屋淸珙) in Jiangnan(江南) region. After returning in 1352, he taught at temples including Seonggaksa in Gaegyeong, Singwangsa in Haeju, and Seongbulsan in Pyeongju, engaging in wide-ranging religious exchanges. Following his death in 1374, his disciples perpetuated his teachings through the 1377 metal type edition of Jikji simche yojeol and the 1378 woodblock editions of Jikji and Baegun hwasang eorok, establishing his lineage’s legitimacy. It is expected that a reexamination of Baegun's life and activities will serve as basic data for understanding trends in the Buddhist community in the late Goryeo Dynasty.

articles.title_kr: 『불교대전』 그 성격의 검토 - 1929년 『불교』 제61호에 실린 「禪敎兩宗聖典編纂과 그 材料精選에 就하야」와 관련하여 -
articles.title_en: Review of the nature of the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) - Regarding the article “On the Compilation of the Canons of the Two Schools of Zen and Teaching Buddhism(禪敎兩宗) and the Selection of Texts” by Sahusaeng(獅吼生) in the 61st issue of “Buddhism(佛敎)” in 1929 -
articles.abstract_kr: Research on Manhae's the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) can be said to have changed a lot since 2002, when the existence of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典) became known in Korea. This is because the similarity of list names between the two books presented by Park Po-ri was so obvious. However, there was no claim in Korea that the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) was a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典). Rather, there was a claim that it was not a translation, and there was no research responding to this argument. In 2023, the article “On the Compilation of the Canons of the Two Schools of Zen and Teaching Buddhism(禪敎兩宗) and the Selection of Texts” by Sahusaeng (獅吼生) in the 61st issue of “Buddhism(佛敎)” in 1929, was discovered in Korea. This is a notable event for two reasons. First, the existence of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典) was already known in Korea in 1929. Second, in that text, Sahusaeng(獅吼生) says that the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) is a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典).Therefore, this paper examines whether the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) can truly be considered a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典). First, compared the citations of the part warning against alcohol(誡酒), after that, compared the Pali and Sanskrit part of the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) with the original text, and finally compared the changes in the sources and citations. As a result, we could see that Sahusaeng(獅吼生)’s claim was not wrong. However, even though it is a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典) for many parts, if we note that he Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) is newly composed and approached from the perspective of Gateway of the Holy Path (聖道門) changing the Gateway of the Pure Land (浄土門) approach of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典), we conclude that its relative originality is still valid.
keywords_kr: 「선교양종 성전편찬(禪敎兩宗聖典編纂)과 그 재료정선(材料精選)에 취(就)하야」
keywords_en: “On the Compilation of the Canons of the Two Schools of Zen and Teaching Buddhism(禪敎兩宗) and the Selection of Texts”

articles.title_kr: 담양 보리암 목조아미타삼존상의 발원문 분석과 조각승 계보
articles.title_en: Analyses of the Balwonmun of the Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple in Damyang and the Genealogy of Sculptor Monk
articles.abstract_kr: This paper analyzes Balwonmun on Restoration of the Wooden Amitabha Triad (1692) at Boriam Temple in Damyang, which describes the creation of statues in 1630. It also traces the genealogy of the assistant sculptors who, along with the head sculptor Na Gyun, participated in the creation of Buddhist statues. The Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam was created in 1630 and underwent four restorations: in 1692, 1914, 1977, and 1982. The original Balwonmun on the Creation of Statues does not exist separately, its contents are recorded in the Balwonmun on Restoration written in 1692.The sculptors who created the Boriam Wooden Amitabha Triad were Na-Gyun, Noe-Hyeong, and Beop-Ran. Head sculptor Na-Gyun is the first to be identified among the sculptors active in the late Joseon Dynasty. The second and third assistant sculptors Noe-Hyeong and Beop-Ran belonged to the Su-Yeonpa school.This study focused on the connections between the sculptors who created the statues of the Myeongbujeon Hall at Muryangsa Temple in Buyeo, a connection that has been overlooked in previous studies. This is because Noe-Hyeong and Beop-Ran, who worked with the head sculptor Ui-Eom on the Myeongbujeon Hall statues at Muryangsa Temple in 1640, also participated in the creation of the wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple in Damyang. Based on this, the lineage of the sculptors who created the Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple is assumed to be from the Su-Yeon School. While the activities of head sculptor Na- Gyun are not well known, Ui-Eom, Noe-Hyeong, and Beop-Ran collaborated with Su-Yeon and other sculptors of Su-Yeon School, and the Buddhist statues they produced reflect the characteristics of the Su-Yeon School.The Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple in Damyang, created in the early 17th century, was authenticated by So-Yo Tae-Neung, who served in the Ui-seung-gun (Buddhist Monk Army). The sculptors belong to the Su-Yeon School, and the observation of head sculptor Na-Gyun's activities provides valuable information for the study of Buddhist sculpture in the late Joseon Dynasty.

articles.title_kr: 무심천수륙재의 시대적 타당성 - 내포와 외연을 중심으로 -
articles.title_en: The Contemporary Relevance of the Musimcheon Suryukjae: Focusing on Its Connotation and Denotation
articles.abstract_kr: This study focuses the Musimcheon-Suryukjae a collaborative Buddhist ritual supported by more than 150 temples within the Chungbuk area of the Taego Order. An outdoor dining place was set up across from the main altar and served without discrimination to participants and local citizens. This clearly shows an example of practicing the meaning of ‘equal offerings’, with the contributions of many people, this shows how the Buddhist community came together with a shared purpose and cooperative spirit.Practicing and setting up altars in Musimcheon-Suryukjae served memorial rites for local ancestors such as Baekun-hawsang and Younggye-daesa,giving the Musimcheon-Suryukjae both historical and regional characteristics. It is decorated with Buddhist sounds, beompae and a traditional gesture, Jakbeop. Unlike general suryukjae, it is performed by practitioners who have learned Beompae and Jakbeop at Wonyong Buddhist institute, so it has a strong sense of tradition, local identity, and independence.After the 1960s and 1970s, Musimcheon-Suryukjae included various rituals like Yongwangje, Yeongsanjae, Yudeungje, Topdol, Yeongryeong - Gohon Uiryeongjae. After the 2000s, at the time of stability, it was reborn in the process of transmitting and inheriting local traditions such as Beompae and the validity of the times is definite.
keywords_en: Chungbuk Administration Office of the Korean Buddhist Taego Order

articles.title_kr: 인도철학의 생애 단계론을 통해 본 평생교육의 방향과 목표
articles.title_en: Directions and Goals of Lifelong Education through the Indian Philosophical Theory of Life Stages
articles.abstract_kr: This paper explores the direction of lifelong education in contemporary universities, drawing on the āśrama model, an ideal framework of life-span development presented in Indian philosophy. According to UNESCO research reports, lifelong education has become a global and historical imperative for humanity. However, in South Korea, lifelong education has revealed various conflicts and issues as it has been incorporated into the formal curricula of universities. These problems stem from the uncritical application of educational systems originally designed for school-age students to adult learners, without a deeper philosophical insight into the essence of lifelong education.The āśrama system (Indian life stage philosophy) offers a model for setting life goals according to different stages of life, providing valuable philosophical insight for shaping the direction and objectives of lifelong education. It divides human life into four major stages, each with its own set of essential goals, to be achieved sequentially. This model views human life from a life-span developmental perspective, proposing appropriate educational content and goals for each stage, and ultimately promoting an attitude that dignifies the entirety of one’s life.The primary participants of lifelong education are middle-aged and older adults who have concluded their socio-economic activities. It is crucial to recognize that lifelong education is fundamentally intended for individuals who have withdrawn from worldly engagements. The āśrama system implies that at this stage of life, individuals should live an ascetic life, dedicating time to the study of classical texts, contemplation, and meditation. This is precisely why philosophy-along with literature, history, and other humanities-should constitute the core direction and content of university-based lifelong education.

1권 호.title_en: Research of Present Condition and Subject of Reform Movement of Korean Buddhism under the Rule of Japanese Imperialism
1권 호.abstract_kr: After the opening of a port in 1876, the Japanese imperialism governed Korean Buddhism to use Japanese Buddhism. The result, many tradition of Korean Buddhism was collapsed. In this time, reform movement of Buddhism appears in objective it conquers the contradiction of Korean Buddhism and it presents a new idea, This reform movement happened from the multi field, The various activity which the renovation of Buddhist Order and Buddhism education of the renovation people became accomplished. Currently like this research was started from 1970`s. In after real research is advanced is 1980`s, 1990`s it developed rapidly. But when it came to 2000`s the research result decreased. To solved these problems It is necessary to joint research in anther fields that magnification of specialty researcher, the collection of data which is published from Japan and the research which is close it relates with the Japanese situation.
keywords_en: Young man`s association of Chosun Buddhism

1권 호.title_kr: 일제시대 불교계 인물들에 대한 연구 성과와 동향 그리고 앞으로의 과제: 불교 사상에 대한 연구를 중심으로
1권 호.title_en: The Result, Trend and Future Role of Research on Buddhist Monks under Japanese Imperialism
1권 호.abstract_kr: In order to study the result and trend of research focused on studies of the Buddhist philosophy of Buddhist monks while under Japanese imperialism, we first selected the people in the Buddhist circle who will be the subjects of the study. As a result, seven monks were selected as the subjects beginning with the Rev. Gyeongheo and including Yongseong Baek, Hanyeong Park, the Rev. Mangong, the Rev. Hanam, Yongun Han and Sangro Gwon. With regards to the entire collection of documents, those which mentioned Yongun Han made up the largest group. The documents regarding his relationship with Buddhism numbered 106, making up 27.6% of the entire collection. This was out of a total of 765 research documents referring to Yongun Han, Next came the 84 documents on Yongseong Baek, taking up about 21.9%. 31 documents referred to Hanyeong Park, Mangong and Hanam each, comprising 8.1% of the total. Last, 25 documents referred to Sangro Gwon, making up 6.5%. From these statistics, we will be able to estimate the interest in Buddhism of those monks. Next, looking at the available research papers, 88 papers referred to Yongun Han, 35% of the entire collection. Yongseong Baek followed with 53 papers making up about 21.2%. Third was Gyeongheo with 43 papers, making up 17.2%, Next came Hanyeong Park with 21 papers, comprising 8.4%. After that was Mangong with 17 papers, making about 6.8%, followed by Hanam with 15 papers, totaling 6%, and last was Sangro Gwon with 13 papers, making up 5.2% of the papers. From these statistics, we can see that the interest level of professional research on these monks was not that different from the interests of the public in the world of Buddhism. By analyzing the research results on these seven monks, we could see the research tasks needed for the future. First, the Buddhist circle, especially the involvement of different Buddhists sects and academia on modern and present Buddhism, is definitely needed. And these interests should be followed up with professional researchers and open lectures on modern and present Buddhism. Second, collecting good data on Buddhism for the last hundred years and its systematic research is necessary. Third, cooperative research among academia is necessary. Fourth, basic research surveying the Japanese religious policy under Japanese imperialism is necessary, Fifth, research on the monks philosophy and activities in the modern and present era related to national movement, independent movement, and anti-feudalism movement is necessary, Sixth, a future-oriented Buddhist historical view that modern Buddhism had, needs to be exposed.

1권 호.title_en: The Trends of and the Problems from the Study of Pro-Japanese Buddhism
1권 호.abstract_kr: I tried to analysis the trends of study of pro-Japanese Buddhism in essay. On the basis of this, I made arrangement the problems and the suggestion from the study of pro-Japanese Buddhism. Firstly, the biggest setback that the study of pro-Japanese Buddhism receive is restriction from it`s religious body. This is the problem result from that Buddhist religious body is not at liberty to discuss the history of pro-Japanese, as resulting from it`s senses of history and the interests around clan. Secondly, one conduct the researches in pro-Japanese Buddhism must gain in number. This is closely related to the understanding Buddhist religious body takes of it`s pro-Japanese work. Thirdly, it is absolutely necessary for the itemized discussion according to subject in study to spread and to deepen. And It is essential that the materials for study are gathered together into a whole. Further, the pro-Japanese acts of Buddhist religious body must be wrote down in the history of Buddhism. The fourthly, the antihistorical and antiBuddhist acts that place the pro-Japanese priest his among a leading spirit or a nationalist, must stop immediately. Even one does something of the kind comes in for sharp criticism. The fifth, not to mention descendant of the pro-Japanese priest, Buddhist religious body must do a selfexamination for and make a confession of pro-Japanese acts.

1권 호.title_kr: 일제의 불교정책에 관한 연구 성과와 과제
1권 호.title_en: Research Result and the Subject Regarding the Buddhism Policy of Japanese Colony
1권 호.abstract_kr: This writing is arranged by the subject and the times of the research result regarding Buddhism policy of Japanese colony and the confrontation aspect of Buddhism group. And it composed of the type which tries to observe the subject which the research against the Buddhism policy of Japanese colony. The statistics of a research result is from 1980`s till 2005. The present research condition shares in 1980`s, 1990`s, 2000`s and tried to observe total 13 editions of master`s thesis and doctorial dissertation and total 17 separate volumes(books). The present research condition tried to observe Buddhism policy of Japanese colony and actuality recognition of initial Buddhism society for starters. First, it tried to observe the actual circumstances of Buddhism society such as permeation process of Japanese Buddhism in the first stage of opening port, change situation of Buddhism society after cancellation of entrance and exit prohibition of the castle town(都城出入禁止令) to buddhist priests in 1895 and actual conditions of buddhism society before and after the order of buddhist temple(寺刹令) in 1911. Second, it investigated the present research condition regarding independence motion of Buddhism society and reform idea, education, a youth movement and organization movement for the head office of Buddhism society. Third, it investigated the present research condition regarding the activity of racial movement and the Buddhism society. It tried to observe the research result with Buddhism society`s research result based on 3.1movement and Sun Hag Won(禪學院) which is constituted with the object to protect Korean traditional Buddhism and nation Buddhism. Forth, it investigated the present research condition regarding pro-Japanese matter which hits Buddhism society. in the first place, it tried to observe the process in collusion with Japanese governing power and the guidance division of buddhism society and remained abuses in the buddhism society under Japanese colony. It is the actual condition that Buddhism policy research of Japanese colony still leaves many research subject. Today, the Buddhism policy of Japan and confrontation of the Korean Buddhism society under Japanese colony is becoming the important disputed point, which is linked directly with present Korean Buddhism, in order to understand Buddhism history in Korea. Accordingly, observing in the meanwhile of research trendy and surveying research task hereafter will be important meaning and I want it helps understanding Korean Buddhism society through like this attempt.
keywords_en: 임제종운동 The Buddhism history of modern age and present age
The present status of Buddhism history research
The policy of religion under Japanese colony

1권 호.title_kr: 일제강점기 불교계의 항일운동 연구 동향과 과제
1권 호.title_en: The Trend and Projects of Research on the Anti: Japanese Movement in the Buddhist Community
1권 호.abstract_kr: The anti-Japanese movement in the Buddhist community during the Japanese ruling period is poor in general in comparison with the anti-Japanese movement in the religious community during this period. This was because the religious body was maintained under a certain level of compromise with the power, although there is a difference in level and individual religious people were free to conduct anti-Japanese movements and activities. Since a systematic response and participation by the religious body were relatively difficult, the scale and intensity of the anti-Japanese movement was relatively poor. In particular, Buddhism was supposed to be disconnected from the world in principle and was expected to be indifferent to worldly affairs; therefore, it was relatively poor in social participation and activity. Therefore, the anti-Japanese movement centering on monks in the Japanese ruling period couldn`t help to be a target of attention, and can even be a more meaningful incident. The historical incident that forms the backbone of the independence movement in the Japanese ruling period was the 1st March Movement in 1919. Among the 33 national representatives who planned this movement, Han Yong-Woon and Baek Yong-Sung participated in the movement as representatives of the Buddhist community. Accordingly, the anti-Japanese movement in the Buddhist community was developed mainly by Han Yong-Woon and Baek Yong-Sung. In particular, Han Yong-Woon organized a movement focusing on young monks in the Joongang Hakrim(中央學林), and those young monks later became the main force of the anti-Japanese movement. Therefore, research on the anti-Japanese movement in the Buddhist community is concentrated on the study about 1st March Movement, Han Yong Woon, and Baek Yong-Sung. It is necessary to conduct research into the process for the spread of the 1st March Movement and individuals who took the initiative in the process, and the relationship with the movement for the annulment of the temple ordinance, which was a law governing Korean Buddhism by Japan, and the later relationship with the movement. It is necessary to focus on the anti-Japanese movement in the Buddhist community and patriotic enlightenment activities of the Buddhist school at the time of the war of the loyalist troops. The anti-Japanese movement in the Buddhist community is the entire resistance movement gainst Japanese imperialism covering the independence movement and the socialist movement. Therefore, research on the Korean monks who performed activities in foreign countries, particularly in China, along with their socialist movement is also significant. At the same time, all resistance against Japanese imperialism included the struggle for justice, public struggle, and armed struggle as well as the cultural movement and the Korean literature study movement; therefore, in a wider sense, the movement for guarding the Buddhist tradition along with the movement for lifting the temple ordinance and an effort to build an independent religious order may be included in the anti-Japanese movement. Consequently, it is necessary to restore the dynamic appearance of the Buddhist community in the Japanese ruling period by identifying the diverse facets of the anti-Japanese movement.

1권 호.title_en: The Foundation and Development of Seonhakwon
1권 호.abstract_kr: Seonhakwon has a important phase in the modern buddhist history. That`s why that Seonhakwon had a important role in the aspect of protection of korean traditional buddhism, inspiration of anti-japanese consciousness, and development of the buddhist cleanup movement. This means that the history of Seonhakwon, the process of its foundation, and those who led a Seonhakwon need to be studied. Seonhakwon was established in 1921 where Japanese colonial buddhism was spreading nationwide. Sunwoo benevolent society was made in 1922 to boost the promotion of Seon for the most Reverend Priest(SuJwa) practicing in the SeonBang. Monks who founded these organizations had strong anti-japanese consciousness and were ambitious for developing the korean buddhism. Therefore the resistant consciousness for japanese law of temple and national consciousness which was influenced by 3.1 movement existed in the foundation of Seonhakwon. Sunwoo benevolent society has the main office in the Seonhakwon and 19 branches all over the country. It was managed by the membership fee of 360 members and donations. But from 1925 Sunwoo benevolent society has gone down because of financial problems. Temporarily Seonhakwon was changed to Kyungsung mission branch of beomeosa and was rebuilt in 1931 by Kim Juk Eum, Then It played a role as a headquaters and made efforts for popularization of buddhism, guiding a meditation, lecturing buddhist doctrines, publishing bulletins. The monks who rebuilt Seonhakwon concentrated on financial settlement for running it. Consequently Seonhakwon was converted into a foundation called Chousn Bulgyo Seonrichamguwon. By the way, the monks used this foundation as a chance of making a organization of SuJwa for promoting Seon, In march 1935 there was a rally of SuJwa in Seonhakwon. SuJwa stands for a unique name called ChosunBulgyo SeonJong, establishing a main office as well as making rules including constitutional law of order. Since then Seonhakwon strived to set up the identity of SeonJong increasing assets and the number of Seonwon. But Seonhakwon was not liberal under the harsh reign at the end of japanese colonization. Inevitably it cooperated with the japanese government because of oppression. But Seonhakwon continued to exist until the liberation although japanese government couldn`t imagine its existence at all. Therefore Seonhakwon has a important mark in modern buddhist history and also its history is a yardstick of grasping the identity of national buddhism including korean buddhism.

1권 호.title_en: The Variation of Character of Seonhakwon after China-Japan War
1권 호.abstract_kr: As Buddhist temple constructed in 1921 by Buddhist monks who had high tendency of anti-Japanese movement, Seonhakwon is highly significant in our modern history of Buddhism. During the age of colony, it was frequented by anti-Japanese monks. In the modern history, it played the role of main center of so-called ``Jeongwhabulsa.`` There is a opinion that Seonhakwonis a Buddhist temple constructed against the Japanese policy of Buddhism. Recognizing that the establishment of Seonhakwon was initiated by monks with high anti-Japanese propensity, I am searching background of construction of Seonhakwon in 1921 from the variation of Japanese colonial policy. It is related to permitting foundation of diverse cultural organizations as Japanese colonial policy was converted from military rule to cultural politics in 1920s. In 1920s, Japan permitted the establishment of cultural organizations in Chosun except politic organization. Japan permitted the establishment of cultural organizations in Chosun as an appeasement policy to cool down anti-Japan movement. As colonial policy was relaxed in this way, Seonhakwon could be established, but it could not actively spread anti-Japan movement, because its activity was confined in the scope approved by Chosun Government-General. Though Seonhakwon was named with the suffix of ``Won(院: temple)`` instead of ``Sa(寺: temple)`` or ``Am(암(庵): small temple)``, it could not be still free from the oppression of power that ruled colony. Seonhakwon was named with suffix of ``Won``, because there was no provision on the establishment of new Buddhist temple in the order of Buddhist temple. Since there was regulation on the establishment of Buddhist temple in the order of Buddhist temple or enforcement rule of order of Buddhist temple, it was impossible to newly establish Buddhist temple. Facing financial difficulty from the end of 1920s``, Seonhakwon was in the crisis of stagnant activity. Thanks to the effort of Kim Jeok Eum, Seonhakwon met the opportunity of restoration in 1931. However, it was difficult for a monk to restore a Seonhakwon with local branch by himself. To solve the financial difficulty, Seonhakwon attempted to establish juridical foundation and was approved to establish ``Joseonbulkyojungangseonrichamguwon`` in 1934. Making use of the opportunity of the 3rd ``Sujwadaewhae(首座大會)`` in 1935, ``Joseonbulkyojungangseonrichamguwon`` established Chosun Zen Buddhism(禪宗). At that time, the establishment of Zen Buddhism was the embodiment of own intent to preserve the tradition of Chosun Buddhism. However, being juridical foundation under the Japanese imperialism means to be subject to the intervention of Chosun Government-General under the system of control. This is because it had to report in writing the result, revenue and disbursement of main project and substitution of directors each year. After Seonhakwon was converted into juridical foundation, it was inevitable to improve relation with juridical foundation, Chosun Buddhism Central Affairs Institute, which was composed of the then head priest of Buddhist temple of 31st center. Furthermore, cooperating to the policy of Government-General, it was forced to leave pro-Japanese traces such as alteration of surname, memorial service for the war dead, payment of contribution for national defense, contribution of metals, etc.

1권 호.title_en: The Historical Foundation in Seonhakwon(禪學院)`s Movement
1권 호.abstract_kr: The establishment of Seonhakwon(禪學院) had something to do with an anti-Japanese character such as Imjejong(臨濟宗)`s movement. Through establishment and restoration, Seonhakwon(禪學院) intended to develop and succeed to a system of three learnings(三學) such as Buddhist commandments(戒), feeling(定) and knowledge(慧). Three learnings(三學) were an originality of Korean Buddhisim. These were a root of vitality, and it was a power that Korean Buddhisim overcame a dismal age. This root came to a crisis, because of japanizing Korean Buddhisim, pressure against Korean Buddhisim and estrangement to Korean Buddhisim. Monks in Korean traditional seonwon(禪院)s and gangwon(講院)s got married, ate meat. So Korean Buddhisim was indifferent to these monks. This was an result, because the place in charge of religious affairs(敎務院) and most head priests of head temples emphasized a school education. In this situation, Seonhakwon(禪學院) provided a wide variety of activities taking a restoration in 1931. These activities were a close connection with a question for Buddhist meditation to get married and eat meat. And these activities succeeded a cleanup movement in Korean Buddhist world after liberation. A trend for monks to get married generalized in Korean Buddhist world of 1920`s. So Buddhist monks with Baek Yong Seong(백용성) entered a protest(建白書) covering double times, and they proposed to prohibit getting married and eating meat. This demand was reappeared in the third Korean Buddhism Most Reverend Priest meeting(朝鮮佛敎首座大會), and Seonhakwon(禪學院) held this meeting in 1935. Seonhakwon(禪學院) intended to overcome the disorder and crisis of Korean Buddhist world, so this was created by a Japanese aggression and an influx of Japanese Buddhism. And Seonhakwon(禪學院) strove to preserve and succeed the originality and subjecthood of Korean Buddhism.
keywords_en: thing to get married and eat meat

2권 호.title_kr: 승조(僧肇)의 ``비유비무(非有非無)`` 논증(論證)과 그 의의(意義)
2권 호.title_en: SengZhao`s Demonstration on FeiYouFeiWu(非有非無) and Its Significance
2권 호.abstract_kr: SengZhao, the disciple of Kumarajiva, succeeded to the idea of Kumarajiva and accomplished Chines Prajna thought. He was interested in the philosophical issues of Xuanxue (玄學) and finally solved the problem of YouWu(有無), which was the most significant one in the philosophy of Xuanxue by the logic of FeiYouFeiWu. In his work, ZhaoLun(肇論), we can recognize that a great deal of phrases are quoted from LaoZi(老子) and ZhuangZi(莊子). Hence, the thought of SengZhao can be considered as the result which is produced by the unification of the Prajna thought in India and the Lao-Zhuang thought in China. The issue of YouWu was the most significant one among the three philosophical systems, namely Confucianism, Buddhism, and Taoism and SengZhao played an important role in solving the philosophical issue. Therefore, SengZhao and his work, ZhaoLun have been considered as the most significant in understanding philosophies in China. The crucial notions of ChuShiErZhen(觸事而眞) and TiYongBuEr(體用不二) etc. which were used by SengZhao, have incessantly influenced sects of Buddhism and both Confucianism and Taoism but the basis of these concepts is placed under the notion of YouWu. It can be said that if SengZhao played a great role in understanding Buddhism, that was because of the notion of YouWu which was solved by SengZhao. In addition, the period of GeYiFoJiao(格義佛敎) terminated when SengZhao criticized the three views of BunWu(本無), XinWu(心無), and JiSe(卽色) and Buddhism came to be studied through its own terms. The disappearance of GeYiFoJiao made Xuanxue declined in China and Buddhism dominated throughout the period of Southen-Northern dynasties in China. This is the significance which the demonstration of FeiYouFeiWu(非有非無) plays a role in the history of thoughts in China.

2권 호.title_kr: 원측(圓測)의 유식사상(唯識思想)과 당대화엄종(唐代華嚴宗)과의 영향관계
2권 호.title_en: Woncheuk`s Vijnana-vada Thought and Avatamsaka School in Tang Dynasty
2권 호.abstract_kr: Korean buddhism was influenced by chinese buddhism. On the contrary, there were a few cases that korean buddhism exerted influence on the formation of chinese buddhism. In this paper, it would be focused upon a fact how Woncheuk(圓測)`s vijnana-vada thought (唯識思想) had an effect on Tang(唐) buddhist society. The new findings are as follows. First, it was given careful consideration to a problem how Woncheuk understood the old translation Buddhism and the new one, both parties were pitted against each other. As a result, he followed Hyeonjang(玄裝)`s new version buddhism in general but he was never opposed to the old version. Second, it was kept an eye on the relation between Woncheuk`s vijnana-vada thought of harmonizing-disputations(和諍) and Beopjang(法藏)`s avatamsaka thought(華嚴思想) of substance-phase(性相) unity. In consequence, it could be understood that Woncheuk`s vijnana-vada thought contributed to the formation of Beopjang`s avatamsaka thought in part, not pitted against each other.

2권 호.title_kr: 조선후기백양사(朝鮮後期白羊寺)의 승역(僧役)에 대한 고찰
2권 호.title_en: A Study on Monk`s Labor of Baekyangsa in Late Chosun Dynasty
2권 호.abstract_kr: Baekyangsa(白羊寺) was established by Saint Yeohwn(如幻禪師) in 632. This temple produced many priestes of virtue from late Koryo dynasty to the present age. Because the Most Reverend Priest Kgkjin(覺眞國師) and monk Chungsu(淸蒐) remodeled Baekyangsa in 14th century, this temple was in full flourish. Baekyangsa Museum has Baekamsa-Jeon-Jang-Su(白巖寺傳帳受) and we can grasp a phases of Baekyangsa in early Chosun dynasty through this book. It is as follows. First, Baekyangsa operated a Temple-treasure(寺院寶). Second, a scale of this temple was over 76 kans. Monk`s labor of Baekyangsa was fallen off or discharged in late Chosun Dynasty. The reason is as follows. This temple was appointed a prayer house for a Royal family(王室願堂) in late Chosun Dynasty. So this temple was benefited in the reduction and exemption about monk`s labor. For example, the queen of Moon-Jung(文定王后) performed a religious service in this temple. A religious service was called as Kuk-Hon-Jea(國魂祭). The queen of In-Heon(仁憲王后) supported this temple, so Won-Moon-Am(雲門庵) established, a Buddhist painting and an image of Buddha ware made. Moreover, this temple had the portrait of the queen. Therefore Baekyangsa was protected by Chosun government.
keywords_en: a prayer house for a Royal family

2권 호.title_kr: 중국 근대불교의 성격과 그 특징 -대승불교, 민족불교 및 근대의식-
2권 호.title_en: The Character and Features of Buddhism in Modern China: Mahayana-Buddhism, Nationalistic Buddhism and Modern Consciousness
2권 호.abstract_kr: The essay is focused upon explicating how the Buddhism in modern China played a vital role in satisfying the comprehensive need of the Chinese community in general, which revealed from the fusion of western culture into the traditional cultures of Confucianism, Daoism and Buddhism. What is called the nationalistic Buddhism comes from the slogan of the wealth and military power of a nation and the survival of its people, the Chinese intellectuals advocated such social reform as the enlightenment of people, the abolition of class distinctions and the abolishment of racialism and feudalism. In order to support it, the essay mentions the contemporary representative heroes of Yu-wei Kang, Ji-chao Liang and Tai-yan Zhang. They constituted the administrativistic view of world, which is characteristic of national administration and its application. With the help of these Buddhistic conceptions, Chinese people had the modern thought of reformation, that is, the self-consciousness of requesting the equal right of people, the freedom and will of individuals, the survival of people, etc, We can summarize how the nationalistic Buddhism could rise and what was its character as follows: First, the nationalistic Buddhism strengthened the awakening of Chinese community through the spirit of contradiction. Second, it vindicated the consciousness of people-right in the recognition of non-discriminative equality of people. Third, it argued the nationalism of defending the Chinese country in the dimension of the salivation of people. In particular, the nationalism of defending and saving the Chinese country was a representative exemplar of revealing the modernization of Buddhism in China. It reflected a kind of turn to the modernization of China, which is closely connected with the Buddhistic character of separating from the worldly reality to that of participating in the worldly reality.

2권 호.title_en: Beomeosa Temple Phase and the Headquarters Temple of the Seon Buddhism
2권 호.abstract_kr: This paper focuse on Beomeosa temple phase of the construct and character in the history modern, Beomeosa temple has representative Pusan buddhism and the headquarters temple of the seon buddhism. Thereupon this paper summarize on the Beomeosa temple phase of the construct and character in the history modern. First, Beomeosa temple hold a large numbers seon metting 19th (1899~1911). In this situtation, suza on the whole country buddhism coming Beomeosa temple. the result, Beomeosa temple turnover representative seon buddhism. And, Beomeosa temple opening to the public of the first temple seon buddhism. After, constructing on the Japenese law of the temple that the headquarters temple of the seon buddhism. Therefore, Beomeosa temple phase connected the headquarters temple of the seon buddhism. Second, Beomeosa temple phase connect to do with an anti-Japenese character such as Imjeong movement. Imjeong movement of the opening part that Jeonrado, And the movement fundamental rules turning Beomeosa temple, Why, Beomeosa temple of the headquarters temple of the seon buddhism and economy power, Third, Beomeosa temple phase action the establishment of Seonhakwon. Beomeosa temple monk particpated of the establishment of Seonhakwon in 1921~1924, This particpate contents man-power of the role construct and economy support, This direction continuance 1930~1945, Seonhakwon of the reconstruction and conversion on a foundation the seonrichamguwon, This point, Beomeosa temple and Beomeosa temple of monk take part in Seonhakwon hard core role of the difficult situation. Eventuly, Beomeosa temple phase constructed the headquarters temple of the seon buddhism in the modern period. The headquarters temple of the seon buddhism becoming Beomeosa temple of the history and character.
keywords_en: the headquarters temple of the seon buddhism

2권 호.title_kr: 한국사회에서의 불교에 대한 신뢰와 불신에 대한 토착심리학적 분석
2권 호.title_en: Perception of trust and distrust of Buddhism in Korea: Indigenous psychological analysis
2권 호.abstract_kr: The purpose of this study is to examine the perception of trust and distrust of Buddhism in Korea. A total of 532 participants completed a survey developed by the present author. In the first part of the study, an open-ended questionnaire asked the respondents to list the reasons why they trusted and distrusted Buddhism. In the second part of this study, the author examined the generational differences adherents and non-adherents. The results are as follows. First, participants trust Buddhism since it represents the historical and traditional religion in Korea. Second, participants report distrusting buddhists since their contribution to society is relatively small and due to their factional strife. Third, buddhist are the highest trust to Buddhism, but christian are the lowest trust to Buddhism, This results represent Buddhism play roles for their missions, and lots of Korean react on trust and distrust of buddhism very sensibly, importantly, truly.
