Compared to the original version, there are some missing contents in the Mongolian version of the Diamond Sutra, which seem to have been omitted because they overlap with the immediately preceding contents. The Sanskrit word saṃjñā was translated as “sedkiküi” in the Mongolian text, and the arrangement order of the four sedkiküi is different from the Kumarajiva’s translation.In relation to the sanskrit text, sanskrit nouns were transliterated in the Mongolian version of the Diamond Sutra, and words appearing in the Tibetan version of the Diamond Sutra were also transliterated into Mongolian.The Mongolian people appear to have placed great importance on the recitation of dharani in the Diamond Sutra. The Mongolian version of the Diamond Sutra contains dharani that is not in the sanskrit text. This dharani is also present in the Tibetan version of the Diamond Sutra, but not in the Beijing edition of the Tibetan Tripitaka. Among the Chinese translations, there is a short dharani in the Kumarajiva’s translation. Dharani was written in the Mongolian version of the Diamond Sutra and widely distributed. I think that it is an example of the Dharani belief in the Diamond Sutra of the nomadic peoples of North Asia.
keywords_en: the Mongolian version of the Diamond Sutra
Tibetan versions of the Diamond Sutra

36권 호.title_kr: 원주지역 불교 역사와 특징 小考
36권 호.title_en: A Study on the History of Buddhism in Wonju and Its Characteristics
36권 호.abstract_kr: 본고는 지역불교 연구의 하나로, 한반도의 중앙에 위치한 원주 지역의 불교역사를 살펴보고 각종 불교문화 유산을 통해 그 특징을 파악하고자 한다. 삼국의 접경지이면서 교통의 요지였던 원주는 차례로 고구려, 백제, 신라의 영토가 되었고, 통일 이후에는 신라 5소경 중 중원경이 설치되기도 하였다. 고려시대의 원주는 국사, 왕사가 주석한 사찰들로 인해 한국불교사에서 중요한 위치를 차지하였다. 고려 초기에 희양산문의 지증 도헌은 거돈사를 창건하였고, 봉림산문의 진공 충담은 흥법사에서 입적하였다. 고려 중기에는 법상종의 지광 해린이 법천사를 하산소로 삼기도 했다. 원주에는 또한 치악산을 배경으로 하여 구룡사, 국형사, 상원사 등의 전통사찰이 즐비하며, 경순왕과 마의태자 전설이 깃든 미륵산 마애불을 중심으로 한 미륵신앙도 특기할 만하다.연세대학교의 기독교 유지나 용소막 성당 등의 천주교 성지로 인해, 얼핏 보기에 원주의 불교세가 약해 보이지만, 전역에 산재한 불교 유적이나 각종 문화유산으로 보면 결코 그 무게가 가볍지 않다. 이에 한국사와 원주 지역사, 한국불교사와 원주 불교사의 바탕 위에, 원주불교의 유ㆍ무형 유산을 종합적으로 고찰하여 원주불교의 보편성과 특수성을 드러내고자 한다.
36권 호.abstract_en: This paper is a study of local Buddhism, and it examines the history of Buddhism in the Wonju region, located in the center of the Korean Peninsula, and tries to understand its characteristics through various Buddhist cultural heritages.Wonju, which was the border area of the three kingdoms, was ruled by Baekje, Goguryeo, and Silla in turn, and after reunification, it was a key point of transportation, the Jungwongyeong(中原京) was installed of the five small capitals of Silla.Wonju in the Goryeo period holds an important place in the history of Korean Buddhism due to the temples annotated by the royal priests(國師).Ji Jeong Doheon(智證 道憲) of Heeyangsanmun(曦陽山門) founded Jūdùnsì(居頓寺), and Jingong Chungdam(眞空 忠湛) of Bongrimsanmun(鳳林山門) passed away at Xìngfăsì(興法寺).In the mid-Goryeo period, Jigwang Hae-rin(海麟), the Beopsangjong(法相宗), spent the last days of his life there.In Wonju Chiaksan  Mountain, there are many traditional temples such as Guryongsa Temple, Gukhyungsa Temple, and Sangwon Temple, etc. In addition, in Wonju, the Mireuksan Maae Buddha(彌勒山 磨崖佛), which has the legend of King Gyeongsoon(敬順王) and Prince Maui(麻衣太子), is centered on the Mireuksan Maae Buddha, and the Mitreya faith is also famous.At first glance, Wonju's Buddhist status seems weak due to Catholic holy sites such as Yongsomak Cathedral, but this is not the case when you look at the Buddhist relics and various cultural heritages scattered throughout the country.Therefore, on the basis of Korean history, Wonju regional history, Korean Buddhism and Wonju Buddhist history, the existence and intangible aspects of Wonju Buddhism will be comprehensively examined, revealing the universality and particularity of Wonju Buddhism, and at the same time, a glimpse into a part of the history of Korean Buddhism.

36권 호.title_kr: 水陸齋會의 設辦과 設行의 主體性 - 용주사 수륙재를 중심으로-
36권 호.title_en: The subjectivity of the setup of the Suryukjaehoe and its performance   - focusing on the Suryukjae at Yongjusa Temple -
36권 호.abstract_kr: 수륙재의 設辦과 設行의 樣態 및 意味와 行爲 속에서 수원 용주사 수륙재의 위상을 찾아보았다. 1790년 10월 1일 용주사에서 행해진 無遮會는 無遮로 법계 성인과 범부를 청해서 施食함으로써 先王의 冥福을 닦아주고, 齋者의 壽福 增長을 위한 목적으로 행해진 수륙재이며, 그 疏文의 ‘謹命’은 재자와 병법 아사리의 위치를 밝혀주는데, 재자는 병법 아사리에게 재회를 열라고 명령하는 위치에 있으므로, 용주사 수륙재는 內行 또는 國行의 수륙재임을 의미한다.용주사 수륙재가 조선 후기 국왕에 의해 행해진 수륙재이므로 정체성에 부합하는 12단 혹은 17단을 설치하고, 宗室位를 중위에 모셔야 하며, 혼령을 목욕하는 浴所도 구분되어야 한다. 수륙재 儀文의 臺詞에는 첫째 붓다가 齋者에게 告하는 것, 둘째, 齋者가 神佛에게 소원을 아뢰는 것, 셋째 法師가 의례를 진행하며 설명하는 것으로 이뤄졌는데, 그 속에는 수륙재가 國行的인 위상임을 알려준다. 정조가 부친의 재궁으로 창건하고 佛像 점안식 날에 행한 용주사 수륙재는 여느 사찰의 그것과 또 다른 분명한 역사와 명분을 가지고 있다.
36권 호.abstract_en: This writing considers the status of the Suryukjae (水陸齋, the offering ritual for land and water) at Yongjusa Temple in Suwon, focusing on the meanings and actions involved in the aspects of its setup and performance. Muchahoe (無遮會; Buddhist ceremony without restriction) held at Yongjusa Temple on October 1, 1790, was a Suryukjae conducted to rest in peace of the late king and to pray for longevity and good fortune. This ritual invited both the enlightened beings of the Dharma realm and ordinary beings to partake in the food offering (施食). The polite request in the text to disclose the deceased’s guilt clarifies the positions of the ritual protagonist and the monks guiding the young monastic. It indicates that the ritual protagonist had the authority to command the monks to conduct the ritual, signifying that Suryukjae at Yongjusa Temple was an internal or national ritual.Suryukjae at Yongjusa Temple, established by a king in the late Joseon dynasty, should have a structure of either 12 or 17 tiers by its identity. The memorial tablets for royal family members should be placed in the middle, and a separate bathing area for purifying the spirits should also be designated. The lines of Its ritual oration consist of three parts: first, Buddha informs the ritual protagonist; second, the ritual protagonist makes wishes to deities and Buddhas; third, a dharma teacher conducts the ritual and provides explanations. This shows that Suryukjae has the status of the national ritual. Established as a memorial temple for his father by King Jeongjo and conducted on the day of the ceremony of dotting the eyes on Buddha’s statue, Suryukjae at Yongjusa Temple has a distinct history and legitimacy different from those of other temples.
keywords_en: the offering                ritual for land and water)
the text to disclose the deceased’s guilt(疏文)
The                 memorial tablets for royal family members
the ceremony of dotting the eyes(點眼式)

36권 호.title_kr: 초기 불교 연민의 현대적 적용에 대한 고찰 -연민중심치료(Compassion focused therapy)를 중심으로-
36권 호.title_en: A study on the Modern Application of Early Buddhist Compassion.  - Focusing on comparison with Compassion focused therapy -
36권 호.abstract_kr: 본 연구의 목적은 초기 불교 연민 수행의 특징과 서양 연민 명상 프로그램의 내용을 비교 검토하여 불교 연민의 현대적 적용을 조명함에 있다. 이를 통해 연민 명상 프로그램에서 불교 치유의 원리를 탐구하고, 현대사회에서의 불교 연민 실천의 가치를 제시하고자 한다. 불교는 전미개오(轉迷開悟)와 이고득락(離苦得樂)을 지향하며, 자신과 타인의 고통을 소멸하기 위한 연민 수행을 강조한다. 현대사회에서 서양의 연민 명상 프로그램은 이러한 불교 수행의 연민 기제를 명상에 적극 활용하여 인간의 정서적 고통의 극복을 통해 심신의 행복을 추구하는 공통의 목표를 갖고 있다. 따라서 본 논문은 중생의 고통 해결을 목표로 하는 불교의 정체성이 현대인의 불안과 상실의 문제를 보듬고 치유할 수 있는 서구 연민 명상에 어떻게 적용되고 있는지를 주목하였다.초기 불교 연민 수행은 수행자의 계행(戒行)의 확립을 통해 이루어진 자애를 기반으로 한다. 이러한 자애의 마음은 욕망으로 인한 나와 타인의 고통을 따뜻하게 공감하게 해주고, 이러한 고통을 나누고자 하는 연민심을 드러나게 하여, 나와 남을 친절을 통해 연결함으로써 삼라만상이 연기적 관계에 있음을 통찰하게 한다. 이러한 불교의 연민 수행을 적용한 서구의 연민 명상 중 CFT는 어린 시절의 자기비판과 자기비난의 내적 상처를 치료하기 위해서는 먼저 자신의 정서적 고통과 연결될 필요가 있으며, 그 연결은 자기연민으로 가능함을 제시한다. CFT는 이러한 연민의 역량을 구축하여 연민이 단지 정서적 요소에 그치는 것이 아니라 인지적 요소의 변화를 통해 구체적인 행동으로까지 전개될 수 있음을 보여준다. 이러한 인류의 보편적인 연민의 마음이 동, 서 융합의 적용을 통해 보다 활발히 계발되고 실용화되기를 기대한다.
36권 호.abstract_en: The purpose of this study is to illuminate the modern application of Buddhist compassion by comparing the characteristics of early Buddhist compassion practice with the content of Western compassion meditation programs. Through this, we aim to explore the principles of Buddhist healing in compassion meditation programs and present the value of Buddhist compassion practice in contemporary society.Buddhism ultimately aims to ‘Turn from ignorance to enlightenment (轉迷開悟)’ and ‘Emancipation from pain and suffering, then attain happinesshe(離苦得樂)’, and especially emphasizes compassion to extinguish the one’s own suffering and the suffering of others. In contemporary society, Western compassion meditation programs actively utilize the compassion principles of Buddhist practice in meditation. This suggests a shared goal between Buddhist compassion practice and Western compassion meditation programs, namely, the pursuit of emotional well-being by overcoming human emotional suffering. Therefore, this paper focuses on how the identity of Buddhism, aimed at resolving the suffering of sentient beings, is being applied to Western compassion meditation programs to address the anxieties and losses faced by modern individuals.Early Buddhist compassion practice is based on cultivating compassion through the establishment of continuous virtuous conduct (戒行) in reality. The compassionate mind enables empathy with one's own and others' suffering and desires, revealing a compassionate attitude to alleviate their suffering. Practitioners connect with themselves and others through kindness, gaining insight into the interconnectedness of all phenomena. Western compassion meditation, applying Buddhist compassion practice, particularly demonstrates through scientific advancements that compassion meditation actively transforms our brains, fostering psychological and emotional development objectively. Among these, Compassion Focused Therapy (CFT) highlights the necessity of healing early self-criticism and internal criticism, fundamental to living a happy life. This healing process requires first connecting with one's emotional suffering, demonstrating the potential for self-compassion. CFT constructs the capacity for compassion through the foundation of compassion, extending beyond mere emotional elements to tangible actions through cognitive changes.The power of compassion, which is a universal human intelligence and spiritual value, transcends all boundaries such as religion, culture, and language, and therefore can be widely applied. Thus, it is hoped that the spirit of compassion, through the fusion of East and West, will be developed and put into practice.

36권 호.title_kr: 예천 용문사 목각아미타설법상의 도상과 주역의 8괘상 및 12벽괘상의 불교적 해석
36권 호.title_en: Study on the images of the Wooden Amitabha Buddha Altarpiece of Yongmunsa Temple in Yecheon, and the meaning of 8-Trigrams and 12-Hexagrams.
36권 호.abstract_kr: 본 논문은 1684년에 조성된 예천 용문사 목각아미타여래설법상의 도상과 본존 아미타여래상 광배에 표현된 󰡔주역󰡕의 8괘와 목각설법상 외곽틀에 새겨진 12벽괘를 분석한 것이다. 용문사 목각설법상을 조성하는데 텍스트 역할을 한 것으로 󰡔예념미타도량참법󰡕을 주목했다. 용문사 목각설법상에 표현된 8대보살의 명칭은 용문사 승려 명연이 1704년에 󰡔예념미타도량참법󰡕의 내용을 발췌해서 만든 󰡔염불보권문󰡕과 일치하고, 참법(懺法)과 깊게 관련되어 있다.목각설법상 본존불 광배의 󰡔주역󰡕 8괘상과 외곽틀의 12벽괘상은 당나라 이통현의 󰡔신화엄경론󰡕 사상에 입각해 분석했다. 아미타여래상 광배의 8괘는 팔대보살을 상징하는 것으로, 외곽틀의 12벽괘는 화엄의 수행 단계로 해석된다.기존 연구에서는 12벽괘의 배치에 대한 여러 견해가 있었다. 그러나, 이는 목각설법상 외곽틀의 12벽괘상 가운데 절반의 수에 해당하는 하단의 괘상들이 중심점에서 회전하면서 보는 시각이 아니라 외부 고정점에서 보는 형태로 상하가 반전되어 표현된 것으로 인한 해석의 오류로 보인다.17세기 예천 용문사를 중심으로 승려와 유학자들이 교류했고, 당시에 유행하고 있던 도교 풍습인 수경신(守庚申)이 행해졌던 장소인 용문사에 목각설법상과 삼존상이 봉안되었다. 이는 목각설법상 외곽틀의 12벽괘상이 당시 불교·유교·도교가 습합된 신앙 형태로 해석된다는 점에서 조선후기 불교미술사 및 불교사에서 매우 중요한 의미를 갖는다.
36권 호.abstract_en: This paper analyzes the images of the ooden Amitabha Buddha Altarpiece at Yongmunsa Temple in Yecheon created in 1684, the 8 trigrams of the Book of Changes expressed on the mandorla of the main Buddha statue, and the 12 hexagrams engraved on the outer frame of the Altarpiece.Attention was paid to ‘禮念彌陀道場懺法(Yenyeom Mitadoryang Chambeop)’ as it played a text role in creating the Wooden Amitabha Buddha Altarpiece of Yongmunsa Temple. The names of the Eight Bodhisattvas expressed in the Altarpiece are consistent with the ‘念佛普勸文(Yeombul Bogwonmun)’ created by Myeongyeon, a monk at Yongmunsa Temple, in 1704 by extracting the contents of ‘禮念彌陀道場懺法(Yenyeom Mitadoryang Chambeop)’, and the ‘念佛普勸文(Yeombul Bogwonmun)’ is deeply related to the method of repentance.The eight trigrams on the mandorla of the Buddha and the twelve hexagrams on the outer frame of the Wooden Amitabha Buddha Altarpiece were analyzed based on the ideas of Lee Tong-hyeon of the Tang Dynasty on the New Avatamsaka Sutra(新華嚴經論). The eight trigrams on the mandorla of the Amitabha Buddha  are interpreted as symbolizing the Eight Bodhisattvas, and the twelve hexagrams on the outer frame are interpreted as the stages of practicing Hwaeom.In previous studies, there were various views on the arrangement of the twelve hexagrams. However, this is an error in interpretation due to the fact that the lower half of the twelve hexagrams on the outer frame of the Wooden Amitabha Buddha Altarpiece are displayed upside down as viewed from an external fixed point, rather than as viewed from a rotating perspective at the center point.In the 17th century, monks and Confucian scholars interacted around Yongmunsa Temple in Yecheon. The Wooden Amitabha Buddha Altarpiece was enshrined at this temple, a place where Sugyeongsin(守庚申; a Taoist custom popular at the time), was performed.This has a very important meaning in the history of Buddhist art and Buddhism in the late Joseon Dynasty in that the twelve hexagrams on the outer frame of the Altarpiece are interpreted as a form of faith that combined Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism at the time.

37권 0호.title_en: A Study on the modern acceptance genealogy of ‘Wonhyo narrative’
37권 0호.abstract_kr: This paper is a study that reveals the modern acceptance genealogy by collectively referring to biography, life history, historical stories, and anecdotes as ‘Wonhyo narrative’. In this regard, this paper assumed a long text, which corresponds to a major inflection point in the style of the ‘Wonhyo narrative’, as the subject of discussion. First, the intermittent phase was examined by analyzing the discourse characteristics of the text, that is, the aspect of narrative and anecdotal representation. Second, the authors' intentions for writing or creation were identified. Based on this, I tried to clarify the nature of the discourse inherent in the text.The modern acceptance of the ‘Wonhyo narrative’, which started with Jang Do-bin's “Great Wonhyo(『偉人元曉』)” and reached Lee Kwang soo's historical novel “Great Buddhist Priest Wonhyo(『元曉大師』)”, has transformed into the spread of enlightenment discourse, popularization of Buddhism, and propaganda of imperial discourse. The media was also different accordingly. The dominant trend was to gradually expand the fictional horizon and seek popularity from biography, which rewritten historical records, to calling the newspaper's historical novel. In conclusion, this paper looked at the beginning of the formation and development process of modern historical literature by tracking the colorful lineage of the ;Wonhyo narrative; that spans the citation or adaptation of historical records and the insertion of fiction.

37권 0호.title_en: A Study on the Poetic Diction of Han Yong-un - Focusing on ‘kkae-chi-go 깨치고’ and ‘cham-eo 참어’ -
37권 0호.abstract_kr: The poem “Nim-ui Chimmuk 님의침묵”, first published in 1926, underwent significant changes in its poetic language through multiple reprints. A central verse in the poem is the second line: “푸른산빗을□치고 단풍나무숩을향하야난 적은길을 거러서 참어□치고 갓슴니다.” In most modern editions, the terms ‘kkae-chi-go □치고’ and ‘cham-eo 참어’ have been revised to ‘kkae-chi-go 깨치고’ and ‘cha-ma 차마’, but the meanings of these revisions are unclear, and it has not been determined whether such changes are appropriate.This study focuses on clarifying the meanings of these two terms by comparing them with Han Yong-un's other poems and works from his contemporaries. I conclude that ‘□치고’ corresponds to the modern verb ‘kkae-teu-li-da 깨트리다’ (to break or shatter), with the subject being the ‘Nim 님’. And ‘참어’ is interpreted as ‘to suppress’, rather than the commonly assumed ‘cannot bear to ~’. Based on this interpretation, the second line can be rewritten as: “The Beloved shattered the green mountain light [representing the worldly love shared with me], walked along the narrow path toward the maple grove [symbolizing transcendental love], suppressed [the sorrow of parting with me], and left me behind.”Furthermore, interpreting ‘푸른산빗’ (green mountain light) and ‘단풍나무숩’ (maple grove) as conventional literary symbols does not align with Han Yong-un's symbolic framework. The phrase “breaking through the green mountain light” and “heading toward the maple grove” signifies breaking free from finite, self - centered worldly love and moving toward infinite, transcendental love within the Buddhist concept of pratītyasamutpāda (dependent origination).

37권 0호.title_en: ‘The origin of the Zen thought system of the Chinese Zen’
37권 0호.abstract_kr: This manuscript takes a look at the origin of the Zen thought appearing in the Mahayana Buddhist scriptures. And the topic is the thought of the Zen sect Zen masters who established the Zen thought in each Zen sect japa by utilizing the Mahayana sutras. Regarding the beginning of the Mahayana Buddhism, as the Buddhism of the Bodhisattva, it is the thought that people can make the Buddhist image through balborishim. Indeed, in the initial scriptures of Mahayana Buddhism, the bongak thought had stood out. In contrast, in the Mahayana scriptures of the middle period, the human nature thought of the physical aspect stands out.Regarding the clean human nature, in ‘Vimalakirti Sutra’, the beonnwejeukbori thought appears. The origin is the Yeorae Sect and the Buddhist sect. Regarding ‘Avatamsaka Sutra’, while emphasizing the seonggi thought, it emphasized that it does not know about the possession of the wisdom and the virtue of the Tathagata on the part of all living beings. [This point is similar to ‘the Seungman Sutra’ and ‘the Tathagatagarbha Sutra’.] In the third, in ‘the Seungman Sutra’, ilbulseung is put forth. As the aspect that all people attain Buddhahood, the sugi has been emphasized. Regarding ‘the Yeoraejang Scripture’ that pertains to the Mahayana Sutras in the middle period has been preaching the Tathagatagarbha. And ‘the Neungga Scripture’ has been preaching the jagakseongji thought. The scripture that had the biggest influence on the establishment of the Zen thought is ‘the Yeolban Scripture’. In this scripture, while saying that there is the Buddha nature in all of the people, it said that the most foolish icchantikas, too, attain Buddhahood. And the women and the evil persons attain Buddhahood. And it said that even the heartless people attain Buddhahood.From after Dharma arrived in China, while the Zen thought was established, the Zen sect was formed. While, mostly, the Zen sect had developed into many schools, regarding the Zen masters of the initial Zen sect, by accommodating the bongak and human nature thought, the Zen thought of the faction of the side was established.

37권 0호.title_en: Features and Significance of Li Tongxuan's Theory of the Six Characteristics (六相說)
37권 0호.abstract_kr: This study explores Li Tongxuan's distinctive interpretation and characteristics of the Six Characteristics Theory (六相說), a core doctrine of East Asian Huayan Buddhism. While previous research remains at a basic level of understanding regarding Li Tongxuan's Six Characteristics Theory, this paper delves deeper to analyze its application, purpose, and structural features, aiming to identify its unique aspects and significance.Li Tongxuan inherited the Six Characteristics Theory from Uisang and Fazang, applying it comprehensively to all phenomena of dependent origination (緣起) and elucidating its essence as unobstructed interpenetration (無礙圓融). However, he does not merely follow their framework; instead, he creatively transforms it, establishing a unique interpretation of the Six Characteristics Theory. Specifically, Li introduces novel perspectives such as the application of the Six Characteristics between doctrinal and practical realms (教法-事法) and the self-application of the Six Characteristics Theory itself, breaking away from the traditional internal structure to propose a more expansive and flexible model.Through these transformations, Li Tongxuan builds an original interpretation of the Six Characteristics Theory, while actively inheriting and developing the theories of Uisang and Fazang through doctrinal reinterpretation and application. This continuity and originality position Li Tongxuan's Six Characteristics Theory as a unique contribution to the intellectual history of East Asian Huayan Buddhism.

37권 0호.title_kr: 원효의 불성유무 화쟁과 일심과의 관계에 대한 연구
37권 0호.title_en: A Study on the Relationship between Wonhyo’s reconciliation of disputes on the Buddha-nature and One Mind
37권 0호.abstract_kr: We looked at the arguments and refutations about the existence of Buddha-nature in Wonhyo's Reconciliation of Disputes in Ten Aspects (十門和諍論). In addition, Wonhyo's reconciliation of disputes was examined, and the relationship between reconciliation of disputes and one One-Mind was examined.In the Reconciliation of Disputes in Ten Aspects, Wonhyo appears to describe the debate and reconciliation of disputes from the perspective of the existence of Buddha-nature, and in the Nirvana Jongyo(涅槃宗要), reconciliation of disputes is discussed from the perspective of the body of Buddha-nature. From the point of view of the existence of Buddha-nature and from the point of view of the body of Buddha-nature, Wonhyo is using the logic of reconciliation of disputes through the aspect of Eui-ji(依持門) and the aspect of Yeon-gi(緣起門). The five-gotras discrimination theory, which uses the natural-pure-seed as the body of Buddha-nature, is reconciled through the aspect of Eui-ji(依持門), and the theory that all beings become Buddhas, which uses Bhūtatathatā as the body of Buddha-nature, is reconciled through the aspect of Yeon-gi(緣起門). It is the position of ordinary categories to considers the natural-pure-seed as the body of Buddha, and it is the position of truthful categories to consider Bhūtatathatā as the body of Buddha.However, Wonhyo sees the body of Buddha-nature with One-Mind. From the point of view of One-Mind, the two arguments are correct in that they partially reveal Buddha-nature. However, since the two arguments do not fully reveal Buddha nature, the two arguments are said to be wrong. In the end, if One-Mind is viewed as the body of Buddha-nature, it is neither wrong nor right.What is the significance of Wonhyo's reconciliation of disputes about Buddha-nature while looking at the body of Buddha-nature with One-mind in modern society? Today, it seems that modern society is mass-producing sentient beings with diverse and complex mental structures. At this point, the significance of the reconciliation of disputes between the theory of five-gotras discrimination and the theory that all beings become Buddhas is that the two arguments act as a practical method from the perspective of One-Mind. In other words, both arguments correspond to ways to lead sentient beings to Buddha-nature.
keywords_en: Reconciliation of Disputes in Ten Aspects

37권 0호.title_kr: 大本 般若波羅蜜多心經의 한역과 티벳역 비교 분석
37권 0호.title_en: Comparative Analysis of Chinese Translation & Tibetan Translation of Large version Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya
37권 0호.abstract_kr: There are two main texts in this study: the Chinese translation of 『佛說聖佛母般若波羅蜜多經』(T0257) & the Tibetan translation of bCom ldan 'das ma shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i snying po/(󰡔世尊母般若波羅蜜多經)(d21). These texts belong to Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya of Large version.The main purpose of this study is to compare and analyze the contents of these two texts. The main part consists of four paragraphs, namely, an overview of Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya, Original text of Chinese Translation & Tibetan Translation of this Sutra and its Korean Translation, and a comparative analysis of the contents of two texts.In addition, the comparative analysis of the contents of two texts is divided into eight sub-items, namely, The name of the Sutra, The expression ‘佛說’ or ‘聖’ at the beginning of the name of the sutra, Format of Beginning and End of Two texts, the number of Bhikkhu in Historical introduction, the meaning of ‘智慧(Shes rab/)’ and ‘Ye shes/’, the addition of the letter ‘Oṃ/’ to Prajñāpāramitā Mantra, the interpretation of ‘世間('Jig rten/)’ in Conclusion, and the adoption of Terminology including the name of Samādhi.In this way, it is hoped that this study will provide new information for a clear understanding of the profound meaning of Prajñāpāramitā hṛdaya as well as for recognizing the differences in content between two texts, and will serve as an opportunity to broaden the horizons of future research on this matter.
keywords_en: Bhodhisattva Mahāsattva the noble lord Avalokiteśvara

37권 0호.title_kr: 대승불교의 계율 옹호론에 대하여 - 『菩薩地』 「眞實義品」에 나타난 소승계 수계의 근거 -
37권 0호.title_en: On the Defense of Monastic Precepts in Mahayana Buddhism - The Theoretical Basis for Accepting Vinaya in the Bodhisattvabhūmi -
37권 0호.abstract_kr: This study aimed to explore the theoretical basis for the acceptance of the monastic rule(Vinaya) among Mahāyānists by examining the “Tattvārthapaṭala” chapter in Bodhisattvabhūmi which is presented by the Yogācāra school. The result of this reseach can be summarized as follows:The Prajñāpāramitāsūtras explicitly state that a bodhisattva should not adhere to the precepts(śīla) of the two vehicles. This reflects the general stance of Mahāyāna Buddhism, which upholds non-self-nature (anātman) or the emptiness(śūnyatā) as their main assertion, ignores the monastic rules.However, while the “Tattvārthapaṭala” in the Bodhisattvabhūmi accepts the doctrine of emptiness as well, this text restricts its interpretation to mean “the absence of intrinsic nature in linguistic expressions,” emphasizing the reality of the basis (vastu) or, the suchness (tathatā).. This perspective critiques the Madhyamaka school’s negation of foundational reality by categorizing it as “misapprehension of emptiness” (durgṛhītā-śūnyatā).It argues that such a misapprehension undermines the monastic traditions and impedes practice; thus, it posits that a practitioner of the Lesser Vehicle, who may hold notions of self (satkāyadṛṣṭi), is preferable to some Mahāyānists with a flawed understanding of emptiness. Furthermore, while ultimate truth transcends by linguistic expressions only, the āgama, as conveyed through transmitted scriptures, are affirmed for their practical efficacy. This modified truth discourse allowed the Yogācāra school to actively integrate the established systems of monastic tradition.

37권 0호.title_kr: 6.25전쟁 시기의 불교 선승들의 동향에 관한 고찰 - 선원 방함록을 중심으로 -
37권 0호.title_en: A Study on the Activities of Buddhist Seon Masters during the Korean War (June 25, 1950) - Focusing on the Seonwon Banghamrok -
37권 0호.abstract_kr: This paper analyzes the activities of Korean Seon masters who dedicated themselves to practice while protecting the essence of Buddhism during the harsh conditions of the Korean War (June 25, 1950) and considers their effects on the modern Korean Buddhism. During the war, many Seon masters migrated south, with Geumjeongsa, Beomeosa, and Seonamsa temples in Busan emerging as key centers for their activities. These circumstances are confirmed through the Banghamrok on Seon Centers and related testimonies. This study analyzes the activities of Seon masters and changes in their practice environments during the war, focusing on Banghamrok on Seon Centers. By analyzing the 『Geumjeongsa Banghamrok on Seon Centers』 and the 「Beomeosa Banghamrok on Seon Centers」, among others, it will explore the war’s impact on the traditions and practices of Seon centers and analyze Seonamsa and other key sites without available Banghamrok records based on testimonies. As a result, this study confirmed that during the Korean War, Seon masters strengthened their unity through practice and interaction and based thereon, laid a crucial foundation for the continuity and development of modern Korean Buddhism. This study reminds us that the efforts of Seon masters to preserve the essence of Buddhism even in the harsh circumstances of the war provide valuable lessons for contemporary Buddhists and that it is important to maintain the essence of Buddhism and continue practice even in any adversity.

37권 0호.title_kr: 간화선의 보편적 적용을 위한 심리치료적 작용기제 고찰
37권 0호.title_en: An Investigation on the Mechanism of Psychotherapeutic Functions for the Universal Application of Ganhwa Seon
37권 0호.abstract_kr: Meditation is attracting attention as a representative measure for the mental and physical health of modern people, and it is actively developing in connection with various Buddhist-based meditation practices and social studies such as psychology. Accordingly, in order to approach Ganhwa Seon(Chan, Zen) as a popular practice method, this paper interpreted the structure and principles of Ganhwa Seon practice in terms of the psychotherapeutic function mechanism within the category of meditation psychology.First, the word, ‘gan’(看, literally, watch (a hwadu)), in Ganhwa Seon encompasses the function of mindfulness (sati, 念), while enhancing the function of concentration and insight through the process of doubt. Based on the internal effect of psychological stability caused by mindfulness, the hwadu doubt has functionally a structure that quickly leads to the hwadu samadhi through the method of concurrent cultivation of samādhi and prajñā(定慧雙修).Second, hwadu investigation which constitutes the core of Ganhwa Seon promotes the arising of doubt through the functions of attention shift and discriminatory consciousness. At the moment of hwadu investigation, the exercise of ‘gan’ primarily separates from unhealthy psychological states and causes conversion to internal insight. At this time the discriminatory consciousness that conflicts with general thoughts leads to the mechanism of doubt. Even if doubt does not arise strongly, it can be expected to have the effect of inducing a shift in attention to the observer’s point of view of metacognition and strengthening his or her own identity and subjectivity.Third, the awareness of problems raised by hwadu investigation that has settled within the practitioner is diverse, ranging from matters facing in daily life to essential inner troubles. The question of what is ‘this’ encompasses horizontal spreading and vertical deepening, and can be applied as a psychological mechanism that connects everyday affairs to a fundamental inner question.

38권 호.title_en: Manhae Han Yong-un’s Doctrine of Buddha-Nature and the “Three Articles of the Agreement”
38권 호.abstract_kr: This paper examines how Manhae Han Yong-un’s doctrine of Buddha-nature (佛性) was philosophically reflected in the “Three Articles of the Agreement” (公約三章), an appendix to the Declaration of Independence proclaimed during the March 1st Independence Movement. In his Treatise on the Reformation of Korean Buddhism (朝鮮佛敎維新論), Manhae sought to reinterpret the concept of Buddha-nature within a framework of modern thought. While referencing Kant’s concept of freedom through the works of Liang Qichao, he ultimately embraced and transcended such ideas from the standpoint of Patriarchal Seon (祖師禪). Manhae emphasized the original equality and autonomy inherent in all beings through the concepts of sudden enlightenment (頓悟) and the realization of freedom, understanding Buddha-nature not as an external metaphysical idea but as the inherent, free, and equal true self (自性) within each individual.This line of thought is concretely embodied in the “Three Articles of the Agreement,” which Manhae is believed to have directly drafted. The first article presents the values of justice, humanity, survival, and dignity, along with an emphasis on a “spirit of freedom,” reflecting his interpretation of Buddha-nature as the manifestation of freedom. The second article can be seen as a natural ethical imperative derived from the concepts of “freedom” and “independence” discussed in the first, while the third article, with its call to “respect order,” metaphorically embodies the spirit of nonviolence.Furthermore, Manhae’s Song of Enlightenment(悟道頌), composed after attaining awakening through Seon practice, symbolizes the realization of freedom, the transcendence of conditioned causality (緣起), and the recognition of one’s original face. It is not merely a personal expression of insight, but a declaration that seeks to awaken the times through a spirit of self-mastery amidst historical darkness. Thus, this study reinterprets the “Three Articles of the Agreement” not simply as a practical guideline for the independence movement, but as a philosophical declaration grounded in Buddhist ontology and ethics of practice, presenting Manhae’s thought as a living philosophy of self-realization and liberation still relevant today.

38권 호.title_kr: 「님의 침묵」에서 ‘침묵’의 사상적 배경: 불이법문  - 만해의 『유마힐소설경강의』를 중심으로 -
38권 호.title_en: The Theoretical Background of 'the Silence' in "My Lord's Silence": The Teaching of Non-duality - Focused on Manhae's Lecture on the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra -
38권 호.abstract_kr: This paper explores the meaning of the silence in Manhae's representative poem, "My Lord's Silence". Manhae has written the Lecture on the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra, which features the 'Vimalakirti's Silence'. This contains Manhae's views on the teaching of non-duality, which can be said to be the background of silence. The results on the book are as follows.First, we looked at the teaching of non-duality spoken at the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra. If silence is at the aspect of Seon(禪), it can be said that the teaching of non-duality is at the aspect of Teachings(敎). The teaching of non-duality refers to the middle way which is based on the theory of dependent origination. This teaching can be seen in most part of the sūtra.Second, through Manhae's commentary on the sūtra, we examined the vivid appearance of the teaching. In the third and fourth chapter, there are scenes in which the Buddha's disciples explain the lessons heard from Vimalakirti in the past. It was confirmed that through Manhae's commentary, he revealed the various types of teaching of non-duality in such lessons.And third, we paid attention to Manhae's commentary on the establishment and practice of the teaching of non-duality. In the fifth chapter, Vimalakirti discusses how a bodhisattva attains a peaceful mind. Manhae showed in the commentary that the teaching has been established through three steps and has been practiced from a passive attitude to an active attitude.
keywords_en: The Lecture on the Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra

38권 호.title_kr: 증각 홍척(證覺 洪陟)과 실상산문(實相山門)의 선풍에 관한 고찰
38권 호.title_en: A Study on the Seon Style of Jeung-gak Hongcheok and Silsangsanmun
38권 호.abstract_kr: 본 연구의 목적은 구산선문 중 하나인 실상산문을 개창한 증각 홍척과 그를 계승한 실상산문 선사들이 보여준 선풍의 특징을 파악하여, 한국 선사상사에서의 위상을 재정립하는 데 있다. 서당 지장에게 남종선을 배운 뒤 신라로 돌아온 홍척은 왕실의 후원 아래 실상사를 중심으로 가장 먼저 선문을 열고 활동하였다. 그의 제자 수철은 왕실과의 교류를 지속하며 실상산문의 발전을 이끌었다. 홍척과 수철에게서 나타나는 실상산문의 사상 경향을 선과 교학, 민간신앙, 현실 참여가 조화롭게 결합된 선풍으로 요약할 수 있다. 이들은 당시 불교계의 주류였던 화엄 교학을 받아들여 선과 교를 겸비했는데, 그 배경에는 서당의 가풍에 대한 계승 의식이 작용했던 것으로 보인다. 또한 산악신앙과 같은 민간신앙적 요소를 배척하지 않고 선법을 전파하는 방편으로 활용했으며, 전법교화의 일환으로서 궁중 설법과 철불 조성 등 현실 참여적 활동을 전개하기도 했다. 홍척을 비롯한 실상산문 선사들은 한국선에서 선교겸수를 표방한 선구적 사례이자, 민간신앙 포용과 현실 참여를 통해 선법의 안착 및 유포에 기여한 공로자들이었다.
keywords_en: combined practice of Seon and Gyo

38권 호.title_en: A Study on The teaching as a Preface(垂示) from “The Story of Have one mind(拈花微笑)”, the second chapter of The Scenery of the true heart(本地風光)
38권 호.abstract_kr: This study is on The teaching as a Preface(垂示) from “The Story of Have one mind(拈花微笑)”, the second chapter of The Scenery of the true heart(本地風光). In the story, when Shakyamuni Buddha raises a flower, Mahākāśyapa smiles. Shakyamuni then declares that he will transmit the Buddha's true Dharma seal and the subtle mind of Nirvana to Kāśyapa. This event serves as the focal point for discussing the Buddha's mind, and the study aims to interpret this story. The reason for focusing on The teaching as a Preface(垂示), because it is emphasized as containing the core message that Master Seongcheol wished to convey.In this study, The hundred days of sermons(百日法門) and he True Path to Zen Enlightenment(禪門正路) are essential references, as they are presented in a logical language. The language of Zen masters often reflects the paradoxical nature of reality, or the simultaneous coexistence of seemingly contradictory aspects. This paradoxical language is the best means to convey the reality witnessed in the state of enlightenment. However, all language can only exist when dividing the indivisible reality into two, which is why The Harmony of Truth becomes necessary.There are two kinds of The Harmony of Truth: one in which the roles of subject and object are separated, unfolding between the interaction of characters; and another linguistic The Harmony of Truth called profound expressions or subtle words(玄言妙句). When the Buddha shows one, Mahākāśyapa responds with two. Through this mutual collaboration, the simultaneous manifestation of wholeness and differentiation occurs. Linguistic collaboration is carried out through poetic parallelism, illogical reasoning, or the fusion with the environment. It holds contradictory aspects together in a unified view. In this way, it reveals the profound truth that the non-self that lets go of the ego is, in fact, the complete revival of all discriminations. Most typically, as seen in the The Story of Have one mind, it is the collaboration between the master and the disciple, or between fellow practitioners. It is also a performance revealing the interdependent arising of the dharma realm, where all things and events are interrelated and rely on each other for their existence.
keywords_en: The Scenery of the true heart(本地風光)
The Story of Have one mind(拈花微笑)
The hundred days of sermons(百日法門)
True Path to Zen Enlightenment(禪門正路)

38권 호.title_kr: 백봉 김기추의 간화선 체험과 선사상적 특징에 대한 고찰
38권 호.title_en: A Study on Baekbong Kim Gichu’s Enlightenment of Ganhwaseon and the Characteristics of his Seon thought
38권 호.abstract_kr: In this study, I examined Baekbong Kim Gichu’s experience of Ganhwaseon and the Characteristics of his Seon thought. First, I discussed Baekbong’s Ganhwaseon experience in relation to the three essentials - Great Faith, Great Determination, and Great Doubt - which are emphasized in the Ganhwaseon tradition. Although Baekbong knew little about the theory and ideology of Seon, and even the methodology of Ganhwaseon, I were able to discover the contents corresponding to The three essentials of Ganhwaseon: Great Faith, Great Determination, and Great Doubt in his experience. Second, I examined the characteristics of his Seon thought centered on ‘emptiness of subtle existence’ and ‘Sentient beings Buddha.’ In this study, I focused on examining these characteristics in detail and examining the basis for these discussions from the standpoint of Seon literature and Seon thought. Baekbong emphasizes that the nature of our mind itself is void-calm, and that although it is emptiness of subtle existence, it itself has a divine knowledge, that is, ‘Numinous-Awareness.’ Also, Baekbong frequently used the term ‘Sentient beings Buddha’ to emphasize that one should practice from the standpoint of Buddha, seeing that many people think of themselves as humble and incompetent. Thirdly, I examined his view of Ganhwaseon focusing on ‘Saemaulgwi’. ‘Saemaulgwi’ means ‘New-Hwadu’ and can be said to be a kind of transformation and reform of the traditional Hwadu. This Saemaulgwi is Baekbong’s transformation of the existing Hwadu centered on monks, He changed that anyone can practice it. This is a substitute for the traditional Ganhwaseon, and it is practiced based on faith in Dharma-kāya rather than doubting the Hwadu.

38권 호.title_kr: 고려전기 의천 편정(編定) 원종문류의 집일(輯佚) 및 유문(類門)
38권 호.title_en: Textual reconstruction(輯佚) and Categorical Sections (類門) of the Wonjong-Munryu, Edited by Uicheon in the Early Goryeo Period
38권 호.abstract_kr: This study investigates the current preservation status, textual reconstruction, and analysis of the categorical sections of Wonjong-Munryu, an essential Huayan Buddhist reference compiled by the Goryeo Uicheon. Presently, only three complete volumes survive: only three volumes(Vol. 1, 14, 22). Partial reconstruction has been made possible through materials preserved abroad. It can be partially reconstructed through citations in Chinese and Japanese Buddhist commentaries from the 12th to 14th centuries. Key sources include Cheongjipgi (聽集記), Simuicho (深意鈔), and manuscripts from Kanazawa Bunko(金澤文庫), which preserve citations of texts otherwise lost in East Asia, such as Yonjun’s Yeon'ocho(演奧抄) and Wŏnrang’s Jipseokgi(集釋記).Among the surviving materials of the Wonjong-Munryu, the ones whose volume order and text names are confirmed are “Bonjong Ogyoryu(本宗五敎類)” in Volume 3, “Jemun Jongchwiryu(諸文宗趣類)” in Volume 7, “Jemun Samsaengryu(諸文三生類)” in Volume 20, and “Jemun Byeoljangryu(諸文別章類)” in Volume 21. Also, Volume 4 is “title unknown”, but it is related to doctrinal classification (教判). Next, the texts of the Wonjong-Munryu whose volume order and contents are unknown are Balsimryu(發心類), Danjangryu(斷障類), Sipjijongyoryu(十地宗要類), Bultoryu(佛土類), and Bulsinryu(佛身類).The Wonjong-Munryu has a philological value in that it systematically preserves the Huayan texts that were circulated in the East Asian Buddhist cultural sphere. In addition, the significance lies in the fact that the Wonjong-Munryu can be used to gauge the academic level of Huayan studies in the Goryeo period and the aspects of Buddhist exchange in East Asia.

38권 호.title_kr: 불교 커뮤니케이션의 학문적 체계 정립을 위한 제언
38권 호.title_en: Suggestions for an Academic Framework for Buddhist Communication
38권 호.abstract_kr: This study conducted an in-depth analysis of the SMCRE model (Source, Message, Channel, Receiver, Effect) in communication studies within a Buddhist context. Through this analysis, we explored new methodologies for effectively conveying Buddhist doctrines and teachings in today's rapidly changing society. The research method involved analysing each of the five components of the model individually and examining the interactions between them to derive the overall characteristics and practical implications of the Buddhist message delivery system. Based on this, the concept of Buddhist communication was systematised.Based on the research results, this study proposed the need to train professional communicators, build digital archives, and establish data-based missionary strategies as core tasks for modern Buddhist missionary work. This study is academically significant in that it promotes interdisciplinary research between Buddhist studies and communication studies and establishes a theoretical foundation for Buddhist missionary strategies appropriate for the digital age.

38권 호.title_kr: 『님의沈默』의 띄어쓰기 양상과 낭송 리듬 분석  - 챗GPT를 활용한 ｢님의沈默｣ 분석을 중심으로 -
38권 호.title_en: An analysis of the spacing patterns and recitation rhythms of “The Silence of the Beloved” -Comparison of Rhythm by Spacing with ChatGPT-
38권 호.abstract_kr: Marking the 100th anniversary of Manhae's publication of “The Silence of the Beloved”, this study aims to identify the gap between the original text and the edition, which has not been sufficiently illuminated so far. In the case of “The Silence of the Beloved”, unlike other poets, spaces have not been reflected in the process of creating editions. There have been many errors in the process of fixing it in modern language, and discussions have been continuously questioned in these editions. To reveal this, this study carefully reviewed previous studies and looked at discussions on spacing. Based on the '萬海學' that many researchers have accumulated, I would like to pay attention to the problem of spacing that has not yet been revealed, and to guess the cause based on Manhae's thoughts and the context of the times, the meaning of spacing in the original text that is not reflected in the modern version.Therefore, this study confirms that the spacing reflected in “The Silence of the Beloved” is implemented as a language art that closely reflects Manhae's inner rhythm and speech sense. In particular, Manhae's "The Silence of the Beloved" is evaluated as a representative work that combines the language reality of the time, the ideological background, and the nature of formal experimentation. It attempts to understand Manhae's spacing as a subjective expression method that reflects the poet's philosophy, way of thinking, and the literary climate of the time. Furthermore, in this study, the spacing of “The Silence of the Beloved” is viewed as a device for poetic breathing and recitation rhythm, and a recitation-based rhythm analysis is introduced using ChatGPT for analysis to compare and examine the differences between the original and the current edition in detail. Through this, we want to reveal the rhythmic and aesthetic functions performed by spacing in poetry, and to re-examine spacing as an essential element of poetic form.

39권 호.title_kr: 만해 한용운 한시에 대한 기초적 검토 - 서지 사항과 번역 문제를 중심으로 -
39권 호.title_en: Chronology, Variants, and Translation in the Sino-Korean Poetry(Han-si) of Manhae Han Yong-un
39권 호.abstract_kr: Although scholarship on Manhae Han Yong-un’s Sino-Korean poetry (han-si) has made some progress, the absence of a foundational critical review has significantly hindered more in-depth research. To address these limitations, this study first examines the bibliographic data, dates of composition, and textual variants of his han-si, and then analyzes issues identified in their translated versions.Regarding bibliographic investigation, this study reconstructs the process through which Manhae’s han-si were compiled. By identifying the sources of his handwritten poetry collection Japjeo (雜著, “Miscellany”) and later compilations, and by comparing them with the extant manuscripts, the study corrects errors that had been introduced in subsequent anthologies.Furthermore, it confirms that the sequence of poems in Japjeo corresponds to their chronological order of composition. This finding is supported by a close reading of Hyangnobongyaeum (香爐庵夜吟, “Night Poem at Hyangno Hermitage”), demonstrating that the chronological arrangement clarifies the interpretive frame of individual works.In the domain of textual comparison, the study shows that mistranslations in Gwannakmaeyugam (觀落梅有感, “Reflections on Falling Plum Blossoms”) can be corrected by consulting its newspaper publication and its later adaptation in sijo form. It also proposes that textual inaccuracies and ambiguities in Jasoshibyeok (自笑詩癖, “Laughing at My Own Poetic Obsession”) can be resolved through intertextual analysis with Manhae’s other han-si and with the works of Park Han-yeong.

39권 호.title_kr: 원효 화쟁론의 생성존재론적 특성과 현대 차이철학
39권 호.title_en: Generative-Ontological Characteristics of Wonhyo’s Hwajaeng Theory and Contemporary Philosophies of Difference
39권 호.abstract_kr: This study aims to clarify the philosophical originality and contemporary significance of Wonhyo’s (617-686) Hwajaeng thought in the context of establishing the identity and global development of Korean Buddhist studies. Wonhyo’s theory of Hwajaeng is not merely a practical mediation between competing doctrinal schools; rather, it constitutes a systematic philosophical framework grounded in the concepts of One Mind (Ilsim) and neither being nor non-being. This research analyzes the hermeneutical features and fourfold negation (Catuṣkoṭi) logic in Wonhyo’s writings and examines their points of resonance with Deleuze’s philosophy of difference and Heidegger’s ontological thought, thereby exploring the possibility of dialogue between Eastern and Western philosophical traditions.Wonhyo’s use of tetralemma to overcome the dichotomy between identity and difference structurally parallels Deleuze’s critique of representation and his notion of univocity. Similarly, the relation of neither-identity-nor-difference between suchness (Tathātā) and arisingand- ceasing within One Mind corresponds to Heidegger’s ontological difference and the event of appropriation (Ereignis). Hwajaeng thought, which affirms difference while seeking interconnection and integration, reveals an inherently dynamic methodology grounded in what may be termed a ‘generative ontology’ - one that emphasizes the dynamic unfolding of being.By situating Wonhyo’s Hwajaeng within these contemporary philosophical contexts, this research seeks to highlight the philosophical potential of Wonhyo’s thought for addressing tensions in today’s pluralistic world and offer significant implications for the global dissemination of Korean Buddhist thought.

39권 호.title_en: The Harmonious Character in Wonhyo's Precepts - Focused on the Essential Note on Observance and Transgression of the Bodhisattva Precepts -
39권 호.abstract_kr: For the past 60 years, there has been a debate in the academic circle of precept on “Why did Wonhyo write the Essential Note on Observance and Transgression of the Bodhisattva Precepts?” I conducted my own research on this issue, and this paper was written to report the results.First of all, Wonhyo made his precepts clear in the book. In the Introduction, he criticized the actions of people who were biased toward external and selfish actions and declared that he would pursue internal motives and altruistic actions. In the chapter of 'Light and Heavy Transgression', he showed in detail that the evaluation of behavior can be changed by various motives based on the Precepts of Yoga. And in the chapter of 'Deep and Shallow Transgression', he reminded us of the importance of altruistic behavior based on the Precepts of Brahma's Net.Moreover, I applied 3 criteria to determine whether the book has a harmonious character: 'the requirements of harmonization' was met because there were confrontations between people with different views on the precepts; 'the appearances of harmonization' did not seem to be met clearly because it is not a harmonious text; and 'the method of harmonization' was considered to correspond to type 3 since Wonhyo decided that one side was right and the other side was wrong. Taken together, it was judged that the book had a considerable degree of harmonious character.
keywords_en: the Essential Note on Observance and Transgression of the Bodhisattva Precepts

39권 호.title_kr: 고려후기 백운 경한의 생애와 행적 재검토
39권 호.title_en: A Reexamination of the Life and Activities of Baekun Gyeonghan in the Late Goryeo Dynasty
39권 호.abstract_kr: This study reexamined the life and activities of Baegun Gyeonghan (1298-1374), a prominent Buddhist monk of late Goryeo, by synthesizing previous scholarship and reassessing unresolved issues. Although research on Baegun began with the discovery of the Baegun hwasang eorok in the 1930s and the identification of the metal type edition of Jikji simche yojeol in the 1970s, the lack of historical materials has limited comprehensive biographical analysis. This paper classifies his life into four periods: (1) ordination and early activities (1298-1350), (2) pilgrimage to Yuan (1350-1352), (3) propagation after returning to Goryeo (1352-1374), and (4) posthumous commemoration. Baegun devoted himself to meditative practice rather than monastic office after passing the state examination and gained official recognition through public Buddhist services such as the 1346 state rainmaking ritual. This status enabled his state-approved study journey to Yuan in 1350, where he studied under Zhigong in Yuan Dadu(大都) and Shiwu Qinggong(石屋淸珙) in Jiangnan(江南) region. After returning in 1352, he taught at temples including Seonggaksa in Gaegyeong, Singwangsa in Haeju, and Seongbulsan in Pyeongju, engaging in wide-ranging religious exchanges. Following his death in 1374, his disciples perpetuated his teachings through the 1377 metal type edition of Jikji simche yojeol and the 1378 woodblock editions of Jikji and Baegun hwasang eorok, establishing his lineage’s legitimacy. It is expected that a reexamination of Baegun's life and activities will serve as basic data for understanding trends in the Buddhist community in the late Goryeo Dynasty.

39권 호.title_kr: 『불교대전』 그 성격의 검토 - 1929년 『불교』 제61호에 실린 「禪敎兩宗聖典編纂과 그 材料精選에 就하야」와 관련하여 -
39권 호.title_en: Review of the nature of the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) - Regarding the article “On the Compilation of the Canons of the Two Schools of Zen and Teaching Buddhism(禪敎兩宗) and the Selection of Texts” by Sahusaeng(獅吼生) in the 61st issue of “Buddhism(佛敎)” in 1929 -
39권 호.abstract_kr: Research on Manhae's the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) can be said to have changed a lot since 2002, when the existence of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典) became known in Korea. This is because the similarity of list names between the two books presented by Park Po-ri was so obvious. However, there was no claim in Korea that the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) was a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典). Rather, there was a claim that it was not a translation, and there was no research responding to this argument. In 2023, the article “On the Compilation of the Canons of the Two Schools of Zen and Teaching Buddhism(禪敎兩宗) and the Selection of Texts” by Sahusaeng (獅吼生) in the 61st issue of “Buddhism(佛敎)” in 1929, was discovered in Korea. This is a notable event for two reasons. First, the existence of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典) was already known in Korea in 1929. Second, in that text, Sahusaeng(獅吼生) says that the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) is a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典).Therefore, this paper examines whether the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) can truly be considered a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典). First, compared the citations of the part warning against alcohol(誡酒), after that, compared the Pali and Sanskrit part of the Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) with the original text, and finally compared the changes in the sources and citations. As a result, we could see that Sahusaeng(獅吼生)’s claim was not wrong. However, even though it is a translation of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典) for many parts, if we note that he Great Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎大典) is newly composed and approached from the perspective of Gateway of the Holy Path (聖道門) changing the Gateway of the Pure Land (浄土門) approach of the Sacred Scripture of Buddhism(佛敎聖典), we conclude that its relative originality is still valid.
keywords_kr: 「선교양종 성전편찬(禪敎兩宗聖典編纂)과 그 재료정선(材料精選)에 취(就)하야」
keywords_en: “On the Compilation of the Canons of the Two Schools of Zen and Teaching Buddhism(禪敎兩宗) and the Selection of Texts”

39권 호.title_kr: 담양 보리암 목조아미타삼존상의 발원문 분석과 조각승 계보
39권 호.title_en: Analyses of the Balwonmun of the Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple in Damyang and the Genealogy of Sculptor Monk
39권 호.abstract_kr: This paper analyzes Balwonmun on Restoration of the Wooden Amitabha Triad (1692) at Boriam Temple in Damyang, which describes the creation of statues in 1630. It also traces the genealogy of the assistant sculptors who, along with the head sculptor Na Gyun, participated in the creation of Buddhist statues. The Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam was created in 1630 and underwent four restorations: in 1692, 1914, 1977, and 1982. The original Balwonmun on the Creation of Statues does not exist separately, its contents are recorded in the Balwonmun on Restoration written in 1692.The sculptors who created the Boriam Wooden Amitabha Triad were Na-Gyun, Noe-Hyeong, and Beop-Ran. Head sculptor Na-Gyun is the first to be identified among the sculptors active in the late Joseon Dynasty. The second and third assistant sculptors Noe-Hyeong and Beop-Ran belonged to the Su-Yeonpa school.This study focused on the connections between the sculptors who created the statues of the Myeongbujeon Hall at Muryangsa Temple in Buyeo, a connection that has been overlooked in previous studies. This is because Noe-Hyeong and Beop-Ran, who worked with the head sculptor Ui-Eom on the Myeongbujeon Hall statues at Muryangsa Temple in 1640, also participated in the creation of the wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple in Damyang. Based on this, the lineage of the sculptors who created the Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple is assumed to be from the Su-Yeon School. While the activities of head sculptor Na- Gyun are not well known, Ui-Eom, Noe-Hyeong, and Beop-Ran collaborated with Su-Yeon and other sculptors of Su-Yeon School, and the Buddhist statues they produced reflect the characteristics of the Su-Yeon School.The Wooden Amitabha Triad at Boriam Temple in Damyang, created in the early 17th century, was authenticated by So-Yo Tae-Neung, who served in the Ui-seung-gun (Buddhist Monk Army). The sculptors belong to the Su-Yeon School, and the observation of head sculptor Na-Gyun's activities provides valuable information for the study of Buddhist sculpture in the late Joseon Dynasty.

39권 호.title_kr: 무심천수륙재의 시대적 타당성 - 내포와 외연을 중심으로 -
39권 호.title_en: The Contemporary Relevance of the Musimcheon Suryukjae: Focusing on Its Connotation and Denotation
39권 호.abstract_kr: This study focuses the Musimcheon-Suryukjae a collaborative Buddhist ritual supported by more than 150 temples within the Chungbuk area of the Taego Order. An outdoor dining place was set up across from the main altar and served without discrimination to participants and local citizens. This clearly shows an example of practicing the meaning of ‘equal offerings’, with the contributions of many people, this shows how the Buddhist community came together with a shared purpose and cooperative spirit.Practicing and setting up altars in Musimcheon-Suryukjae served memorial rites for local ancestors such as Baekun-hawsang and Younggye-daesa,giving the Musimcheon-Suryukjae both historical and regional characteristics. It is decorated with Buddhist sounds, beompae and a traditional gesture, Jakbeop. Unlike general suryukjae, it is performed by practitioners who have learned Beompae and Jakbeop at Wonyong Buddhist institute, so it has a strong sense of tradition, local identity, and independence.After the 1960s and 1970s, Musimcheon-Suryukjae included various rituals like Yongwangje, Yeongsanjae, Yudeungje, Topdol, Yeongryeong - Gohon Uiryeongjae. After the 2000s, at the time of stability, it was reborn in the process of transmitting and inheriting local traditions such as Beompae and the validity of the times is definite.
keywords_en: Chungbuk Administration Office of the Korean Buddhist Taego Order

39권 호.title_kr: 인도철학의 생애 단계론을 통해 본 평생교육의 방향과 목표
39권 호.title_en: Directions and Goals of Lifelong Education through the Indian Philosophical Theory of Life Stages
39권 호.abstract_kr: This paper explores the direction of lifelong education in contemporary universities, drawing on the āśrama model, an ideal framework of life-span development presented in Indian philosophy. According to UNESCO research reports, lifelong education has become a global and historical imperative for humanity. However, in South Korea, lifelong education has revealed various conflicts and issues as it has been incorporated into the formal curricula of universities. These problems stem from the uncritical application of educational systems originally designed for school-age students to adult learners, without a deeper philosophical insight into the essence of lifelong education.The āśrama system (Indian life stage philosophy) offers a model for setting life goals according to different stages of life, providing valuable philosophical insight for shaping the direction and objectives of lifelong education. It divides human life into four major stages, each with its own set of essential goals, to be achieved sequentially. This model views human life from a life-span developmental perspective, proposing appropriate educational content and goals for each stage, and ultimately promoting an attitude that dignifies the entirety of one’s life.The primary participants of lifelong education are middle-aged and older adults who have concluded their socio-economic activities. It is crucial to recognize that lifelong education is fundamentally intended for individuals who have withdrawn from worldly engagements. The āśrama system implies that at this stage of life, individuals should live an ascetic life, dedicating time to the study of classical texts, contemplation, and meditation. This is precisely why philosophy-along with literature, history, and other humanities-should constitute the core direction and content of university-based lifelong education.
